President Donald Trump is pushing to make daylight saving time permanent, arguing that getting rid of the twice-yearly time change would reduce the murder rate across the country.

Trump urged the Senate to “PASS THE SUNSHINE PROTECTION ACT,” which cleared the House last month in a 308-117 vote and would keep daylight saving time permanent instead of shifting the clocks back an hour each fall.

“For many years, the vast Majority of Americans have asked to make Daylight Saving Time permanent, but no Administration has been able to get it properly done, until now. I am proud to announce that the House of Representatives has passed the Bill, and it has now gone to the Senate for final approval,” Trump wrote Wednesday on Truth Social.

The president noted that people are “sick and tired of having to change their clocks twice a year,” and rattled off a wide-ranging list of potential benefits from ending the century-old practice, including reducing crime, improving health, and preventing traffic accidents.

“Leading Medical, Crime, and Economic Studies have shown that ceasing the biannual time change, giving us one extra hour of natural sunlight in the evenings, will help Decrease Robbery and Murder Rates, Reduce Car Accidents (especially those involving Pedestrians!), Lower Risk for Cardiac Issues, Stroke, and Seasonal Depression. Make it Safer for Children to Walk Home from Shool, Increase Time with your Family, Strong Support Extracurricular Activities, Be a Big Boost to Sports, Fitness, Tourism, Retail, and the Restaurant Industries (and more!), and Save Money on Energy Bills, because everyone will be enjoying an EXTRA HOUR OF DAYLIGHT,” Trump wrote.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump is urging the passage of the Sunshine Protection Act, which would make daylight saving time permanent. He is claiming the change would reduce the nation’s murder rate ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. )

Trump added: “In other words, leave it as it is now, and never change again.”

The president then pitched the bill as a bipartisan issue that “Republicans, Dumocrats, and Independents can unite behind.”

As it stands, daylight saving time begins on the second Sunday in March, when clocks move forward by one hour at 2 a.m. The change allows for more sunlight hours during the summer, and when clocks shift back one hour on the first Sunday in November, mornings become lighter.

The system is governed by federal law, though states are not required to follow it. Neither Arizona nor Hawaii observe daylight saving time, and U.S. territories Puerto Rico, Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands also stay on standard time year-round.

Trump ran for president in 2024 on the promise that he would make daylight saving time permanent.

While Trump’s sweeping list of benefits may seem like an oversell, there is some truth to daylight saving time reducing crime rates. When we turn our clocks back in the fall, criminals use the extra hour of darkness to carry out more robberies, according to a 2015 study in The Review of Economics and Statistics.

The study found that when people turn their clocks back in the fall, robberies increase by 7 percent over the whole day — but go up 27 percent in the hours after sunset.

open image in gallery Trump ran for president in 2024 on the promise that he would make daylight saving time permanent ( Copyright 2025 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. )

There’s less evidence, however, to suggest that greater evening daylight reduces the rate of homicides.

One study found that daylight saving time had “no significant effect on changes in homicide rates per 100,000 inhabitants” in the Brazilian state of Rio Grande do Sul.

A 2012 working paper from Stanford found that during daylight saving time there was a decrease in evening murders. However, the paper noted the effect was not statistically significant in the researcher’s analysis.

Another study published in 2024 in the journal Lighting Research & Technology similarly found “mixed” evidence between lighting and crime, reporting no significant connection between daylight and homicide.

However, that study also found much stronger evidence linking additional light to an increase in robberies.

There have been previous pushes to make daylight saving time permanent. In March 2022, the Senate unanimously approved an earlier version of the legislature, but it stalled in the House over whether the country should make daylight saving time or standard time permanent.

News.title: ‘More pain’ to come after economic slowdown
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. The economy grew at a slower pace in the second quarter of the year, official figures show, under pressure from the Iran war.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc between April and June, down from 0.6pc in the first three months of the year, according to the Office for National Statistics.

The figures underline the challenge that the conflict poses for Andy Burnham, who has pledged to deliver “growth in every postcode”.

The Prime Minister has already been warned that the economy will slow further next year if Donald Trump continues his war in the Middle East.

Treasury officials have predicted UK growth of just 0.3pc in 2027 if the Strait of Hormuz stays blocked for the rest of this year.

That is far lower than the 1.6pc predicted by the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) in March, based on assumptions made before the start of the war. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Iran war threatens to cripple growth, Treasury warns Burnham | Officials predict economic expansion of just 0.3pc in 2027 if Strait of Hormuz stays blocked

2) Britain facing £54bn bill for North Sea shutdown | Costs soar amid shortage of specialised ships needed to clear up abandoned oil rigs

3) Ban on zero-hours contracts to cost companies up to £3bn | Businesses face huge bill to offer workers guaranteed hours under Employment Rights Act

4) Nvidia’s AI push has echoes of Enron, says Big Short investor | Michael Burry claims chip giant is engaging in ‘circular’ financing

5) Shadow bank founder battles to stave off bankruptcy threat | Paresh Raja launches legal claim to prevent administrators from chasing him for repayment

What happened overnight

Asian shares were mostly higher, powered by gains for AI-related stocks including computer chips as regional markets tracked a rally on Wall Street.

Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 advanced 1.6pc to 68,601.21. In South Korea, the Kospi jumped 4pc, climbing to 6,844.65, as shares in Samsung Electronics surged 5.4pcc. Computer chipmaker SK Hynix jumped 7.1pc.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose 0.3pc to 3,967.28, while the Shanghai Composite index added 0.5pc to 3,967.65.

In Australia, the S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.4pc to 9,155.80.

Data from the US on Wednesday showed consumer prices had risen in line with analysts’ expectations in July.

Wall Street stocks were boosted on Wednesday by gains made by tech companies CoreWeave and Super Micro Computer, both of which closed up by more than 19pc.

The Nasdaq Composite ended the session up 0.5pc, with the S&P 500 up nearly 0.3pc. The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished the session marginally down.

Oil prices were little changed as investors weighed the deadlock in talks between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, was broadly flat at nearly $89 a barrel.

News.title: H5N1 sparks a very Australian epidemic
News.content:
H5N1 bird flu has reached Australia’s shores and is threatening to infect some of the country’s most unique wildlife.

Australasia is the last continent to be hit by the highly infectious avian influenza H5N1, a new strain of which has been circulating worldwide since 2020.

Since recording its first case in June, more than 200 wild seabirds in Australia have been infected, with fears that the highly infectious flu could quickly ‘jump’ to other species.

While H5N1 has infected animals from foxes to sea lions in other parts of the world in recent years, the epidemic now threatens some of Australia’s most iconic wildlife – many of which are found nowhere else on earth.

An Australian government assessment of more than 2,000 native species warned that nearly one in five faces a high risk from the deadly H5N1 bird flu, with hundreds of unique birds and mammals vulnerable to severe population reductions or even extinction.

Those animals include iconic species like the Tasmanian devils, quolls, and dingoes.

Other aquatic mammals, including the platypus, which is only found in Australia, are at risk of infection through contact with bird droppings in shared wetlands and coastal environments.

News.title: Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end
News.content:
Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

News.title: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG
News.content:
His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

News.title: Advice, cookbooks and emergency pot noodles: Your best gifts for university students
News.content:
When it comes to sending a child or grandchild off to university, it can be tempting to fill their room with every conceivable gadget.

So to help, we asked the Telegraph Recommended Community for their best gift recommendations and their suggestions ranged from desk lamps to cookery books and supermarket gift cards.

Here are the essentials worth buying.

Kitchen basics

From cupboard essentials to electrical appliances and cookbooks, most readers say they’d gift kitchen equipment.

Thinking back to his university days, reader TJ, 43, from London, says “the main essentials are around kitchen items and good long lasting food”.

“It’s nice to have some bits to cook for others as well and to make friends quickly,” he adds.

Susan, 54, from the West Midlands, agrees, recommending “basic cooking equipment” as a key staple and “distinctive cutlery, plates and cups that are easily identified”, which are particularly useful for shared accommodation.

“A box of store cupboard ingredients such as olive oil, soy, stock cubes and spices to use when cooking,” is also well-received, she says.

News.content:
Newcastle 1 Everton 3

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

Inacio, 18, is a Borussia Dortmund starlet who is beginning to make waves since making his first-team debut last season.

The Italian football insider went on to suggest Italy under new manager Roberto Mancini are eager to lock the starlet down before his head can be turned.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea MUST sign Emi Martinez from Aston Villa in rival transfer swoop to become genuine title contenders
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are a top-level goalkeeper away from challenging for the Premier League title, and there is one they should be targeting.

The Blues have spent very well this summer, buying players with Premier League experience who are ready to make the step up to competing for the biggest titles, having shone individually with their former clubs.



The likes of Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers are the best two examples of players from within the league who could infinitely improve in the right environment and become some of the best in the league in their positions.

Look at Joao Pedro, Moises Caicedo, and even Marc Cucurella – Chelsea, when buying from within the Premier League, have a good hit rate of their players becoming top tier.



Of course, in their goalkeeper – Robert Sanchez – they already tried this once.

So what they need to do in goal is not sign someone and hope they will improve, it’s to sign someone who is already world-class.



That someone is Emiliano Martinez of Aston Villa.

I mean, you’ve already taken their most creative player and their set-piece coach – surely Behdad Eghbali could have set up some sort of Buy two get one free deal, no?

The dilemma with Sanchez is, that he’s not that bad.

He is not bad enough that the club desperately need a new goalkeeper because he is constantly throwing the ball in his own net or making stupid errors and not making saves.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Actually he is a fairly solid Premier League keeper – but fairly solid is not going to win you titles.

He is a good shot stopper, who is okay with his feet, and improves drastically when he is playing with confidence, which was personified when Chelsea won the Club World Cup and he genuinely looked like one of the world’s best keepers.

So if Xabi Alonso can instill that level of confidence in him again, then maybe Chelsea will back themselves to win the league with him in between the posts.

That said, they would certainly back themselves a little more if they had a world-class keeper, who has won the World Cup, the Europa League with Villa, and back-to-back Yashin Trophies with several years of Premier League experience as one of the league’s best stoppers.

Not only that, but Martinez just feels so Chelsea – he is the kind of s******** personality that Stamford Bridge would fall in love with.



So why are Chelsea not going out and getting him?

Well firstly, as I said, Sanchez is not THAT bad, or bad enough that the club are desperate to replace him, not in the same way that they needed a centre-back or a left-winger.

The club are happy with their goalkeeping options, including the supposed next best goalkeeper in the world in Mike Penders.

So much so that there is no interest in signing the likes of Diogo Costa from Porto, despite an appreciation of his ability.



They did look into the signing of Mike Maignan from AC Milan last summer as a market opportunity, but the deal couldn’t be made and he signed a new contract in Milan.

Other keepers that they could look into signing, that would be an improvement on Sanchez, include Borussia Dortmund‘s Gregor Kobel, Spain‘s number one Unai Simon, or Roma‘s Mile Svilar.

Maignan and even someone like Jan Oblak from Atletico Madrid could be good options too.

It feels though, as if Chelsea will go into this season with Sanchez as the number one and Penders as the number two, with the Belgian at some point being given a chance to stake his claim in the first team early.

The Spaniard feels like he has Alonso’s backing this term, and claimed that his countryman’s ‘simplicity’ will benefit him, after sometimes struggling to cope with the complexities of playing the goalkeeper role under Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior.



Sanchez said on Alonso: “It is the simplification of things.

“He is allowing me to do what I am best at. I have already played a lot of games in the Premier League and people know what I am good at or not.

“He is allowing me to do what I do best and that means my confidence is going to be boosted and I am going to play better and better. That is what is great about him.”



If things are not so simple by January though, Chelsea could be looking to dip into the goalkeeper market mid-season once more.

Sports.title: Every Premier League kit ranked ahead of 2026/27 season with ‘Teletubby’ shirt tanking and Arsenal missing top spot
Sports.content:
THE new Premier League season is almost here, which means it’s also time to rate and slate every kit for the 2026-27 campaign.

New shirts often generate nearly as much debate as transfers.

And it’s fair to say some clubs have been savaged over their threads this year.



So we’ve decided to jump on the bandwagon and give our own verdict over the latest designs.



Here is SunSport’s official ranking of all 20 Premier League home kits.

20 – Hull City

Starting us off in last place is newly-promoted Hull City, who have come out with, in my humble opinion, an absolute howler of a home kit that looks more like a rugby jersey.

The Tigers have ditched last season’s one-colour body in favour of retro black and orange stripes, but they’ve got a bizarre new logo featuring just the letters HCAFC, which definitely looks odd.



They’ve also got a new kit supplier Oxen – which replaces Kappa – and a new white collar has come in to match the same colour on the sleeves.

Worth a try? If you like rugby, maybe…

Despite our verdict, it appears to have sold out at the club shop, proving we know nothing. The rather tastsy away shirt is available though…



19 – Newcastle

Less a football kit, more an optical illusion. Some fans have dubbed it “the barcode kit” with what the club calls a “bold, disrupted stripe pattern”.

It’s certainly bold, alright, but not in a good way. Gone are Newcastle’s traditional thick black and white stripes in favour of… whatever this is.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

There’s a series of vertical stripes varying in size that spread to the sleeves – with a thick light blue pattern on the shoulder.

It just doesn’t really work and it seems fans agree.



18 – Bournemouth

The tragic thing about Bournemouth’s new home shirt is that it MIGHT have been OK if it didn’t have a giant pink Vitality logo spread across the middle of a black and red striped shirt.

The only problem is: It DOES have a giant pink Vitality logo spread across the middle of a black and red striped shirt. Some have even compared it to something out of the Teletubbies. It’s a shame as well because I like the gold detail on the collarbone.

But the placement, size and colour of the sponsor just absolutely wrecks this kit – which is a shame as it’s Bournemouth’s first season in Europe. Sorry, Cherries.

17 – Leeds

Have you ever spilt sauce down your crisp white T-shirt and tried to wash it out, but you could still see stain left behind? That’s what Leeds’ new kit looks like to me.



The issue is the interesting choice of horizontal blue and yellow pinstripes running aross the body. Yellow and white is always a big no-no when it comes to football kits, for me anyway.

But here the yellow stripes just look messy from afar. I do like the yellow and blue detail around the collar and the blue on the shoulders and sleeves. But the main part of the design is an eyesore. At the very least, maybe it will distract Leeds’ opponents this season.

16 – Crystal Palace

Never been a fan of a seat belt kit and that’s exactly what Palace have done here – moving away from the traditional blue/red combination for the first time since the 2008-09 season.

Instead, the blue/red colours are on the diagonal sash and a similar pattern is seen running across the sleeves too. It actually looks closer to last season’s away kit and doesn’t really feel like a home kit.



Kit sponsor Temporal is also a new addition, as is a re-imagined version of the club crest. Unfortunately it’s just not as strong as recent Palace kits.

15 – Nottingham Forest

What’s this? The first Premier League kit to use tie-dye for their design? No, that’s not happening, but it certainly looks like it.

Forest manufacturers Adidas have gone for a striking all red strip with dark patches blotched all over. It’s a bit of a mess and definitely a downgrade on their elegant 2025-26 kit with white pinstripes.

The simple white stripes on the shoulders are nice but the rest is just too much to look at.



14 – Chelsea

Chelsea‘s new home kit looks simple and decent – until you squint your eyes and realise a giant version of the club’s badge has been imprinted on the body of the shirt.

This might have been a classy, subtle detail if the crest features were much smaller and woven into the fabric. But the whole crest is plastered straight on to the front and the fact there is no kit sponsor draws more attention to it.

I am a fan of the collar and contrast of blue and yellow, plus the nice little yellow slashes on the shoulders. If they get a new front of shirt sponsor this instantly gets elevated a few places.



13 – Everton

Not a bad entry from Everton and an improvement on last year’s home kit that had black horizontal zigzags running through it.

New sponsor CMC Markets has entered the chat in the third shirt designed by Castore. There’s also yellow edge to the white collar and a patch of orange on the sleeve which helps it stand out.

It’s playing it pretty safe so I’m putting it at 13th, which is where Everton finished last season.

12 – Coventry

Safe to say Coventry’s new home strip hasn’t gone down too well with fans. Some have claimed it looks too similar to Sheffield Wednesday.



No doubt, the shirt they wore during their promotion-winning campaign of 2025-26 was much cleaner with an all sky blue colour. This year the club have brought back the blue and white stripes.

I don’t think it’s too bad but the orange Monzo logo running across it doesn’t look great.

11 – Fulham

Another club that has switched out its shirt sponsor as Fulham trades SBO Top for ClickHouse and goes for a black, white and red theme.

It’s a pretty fine kit that doesn’t try to do anything tricky or complicated. Fans have got a neat and simple design that’s pleasing to the eye.



And that’s why it’s in the middle of the range in our rankings.

10 – Ipswich

Not too dissimilar to last season, the Tractor Boys have produced another clean dark blue design with the same Halo front of sponsor logo.

But what shines from this kit is the diamond-shaped pattern across the body of the shirt.

It does the job and it’s nice and tidy. I wish the same could be said about their away shirt – the less said about that, the better.



9 – Brighton

Brighton shirts usually look more or less the same every year. It’s normally a variation of blue and white vertical stripes, so no surprises for guessing they have another variety this season.

I have to say though, I am a fan of the smaller stripes, which have been squeezed into white pinstripes, with a white v-neck at the top.

Brighton are often credited for their stylish performances and consistency and they’re doing the same thing with their kit this season.



8 – Aston Villa

The reigning Europa League champions have gone a shade darker on the burgundy and got rid of the light-blue sleeves, and this is a really nice effort from Adidas.

The blue colour has transitioned to the sleeve and shoulder with a classy new collar.

There’s also a new shirt sponsor with Visit Rwanda replacing Betano for this season. All round it’s a solid entry for the Villans.

7 – Tottenham

Nike have been accused of playing it safe too often with their Tottenham designs – and this season’s kit won’t do anything to change that view.



But what you can’t argue with is that they’ve come up with a nice, clean design that won’t cause too many complaints. There’s a faint diagonal grey striped pattern cutting across the body that helps it stand out.

And the manufacturers have included navy streaks down the sides of the kit, with a unique, layered design of the neck. It scores points for cleanliness but loses points for lack of edginess.

6 – Man City

A new era for the Sky Blues after Pep Guardiola ended his 10-year reign at the Etihad and City have a new kit to match that feels reminiscent of their older editions.

It’s pure light blue all over with a gradient at the bottom that fades it ever so slightly.



There is white trim on the neckline and edges of the sleeves, which makes it look similar to the 2009-10 kit. It will please the purists as the logos are all the same colour, creating a great contrast to the light blue.

5 – Sunderland

I do love it when a club pays homage to a classic kit and that’s exactly what Sunderland have done with their new home shirt.

The Black Cats have come out with what is probably the most visually striking and unique design that is influenced by their 1937 FA Cup-winning kit.

The vintage-style shirt keeps the thick red and white vertical stripes but introduces a pointy collar with the club’s logo protected by an old-school crest. It’s an instant classic as Sunderland play a first season in the Europa League.



4 – Man United

If we were ranking away kits, United would be first place on this list. But their home strip is pretty good too – another clean design with a collar.

The all-red shirt is lovely with a small but eye-catching black and white strip pattern on the collar and sleeve.

It looks like a classic Manchester United shirt design with the Snapdragon logo in white down the front. You won’t get too many complaints about this at all as United prepare for their first full season under Michael Carrick.



3 – Arsenal

They’re the reigning Premier League champions but they don’t quite top the standings on this list, unfortunately.

That’s not to say Arsenal don’t have a very nice looking kit, however, quite the opposite. It feels like an evolution from their title-winning kit as dark stripes are added to the shoulder.

And on the edges of the sleeve and neckline you can see a small red and black pattern that gives it a standout effect.

2 – Liverpool

One of the more ‘out there’ design choices from Adidas, who have created a unique strip that has a firework-style pattern.



The red shirt has little white triangles and lines dotted around that looks like it’s exploding across the kit.

There’s also a red edge around the neckline and white stripes on the shoulder (as seen on many Adidas designs). It’s eye-catching and scores points for bravery.

1 – Brentford

The Bees will be buzzing with this design from Joma – not just because it’s sleek, bold and punchy.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Brentford announced that this will be their kit for the next TWO seasons, which should help avoid fans having to pay obscene prices year after year. Fans across the Prem should have little to critique on this kit and it’s had rave reviews across the board.



Joma have kept things simple with the red and white stripes – but what brings it together are the yellow and black detail around the neckline, sleeves and sides of the kit. It makes the whole thing look eye-popping and it’s the winner for me.

Sports.title: Chelsea ‘land transfer pay-day windfall’ as Romelu Lukaku completes stunning Fenerbahce move from Napoli
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are set to bank a transfer windfall after Romelu Lukaku completed his move from Napoli to Fenerbahce.

The Turkish giants have snapped up the Belgium striker in a deal that will see the Blues benefit thanks to a sell-on clause inserted when they allowed Lukaku to join Napoli two years ago.



The exact transfer fee has not been disclosed, but the Stamford Bridge club are in line for a welcome financial boost from the sale of the 33-year-old.

Lukaku endured an injury-hit campaign last season, making just seven appearances in all competitions for Napoli, but he still managed to add to his reputation as one of Belgium’s greatest-ever forwards by scoring three goals at the World Cup.



The striker, Belgium’s record goalscorer with 93, has now returned to Turkey, a country close to his heart after spending part of his childhood there when his father Roger played for Super Lig side Genclerbirligi.

In a message to Fenerbahce supporters, Lukaku said: “It’s an honour and a privilege to be joining your club.

“I am fit, 100 per cent, ready to go. It is an emotional moment after many years to be going back to Turkey where I lived as a young kid, where I discovered the professional world as a toddler with my dad.”

Lukaku leaves Napoli having won the Serie A title and adds Fenerbahce to a career that has also seen him lift league crowns with Anderlecht and Inter Milan, as well as the Club World Cup with Chelsea.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The move makes him the second former Manchester United forward to join Fenerbahce this summer after Mason Greenwood’s arrival from Marseille.



Fenerbahce, who have finished runners-up to Galatasaray in each of the last four seasons, are chasing their first Turkish league title since 2014, and will hope Lukaku can fire them back to the top.

For Chelsea, the deal provides another boost to their transfer strategy, with the club continuing to benefit from smart clauses included in previous player sales.

Sports.title: Premier League title winner tells Chelsea to raid Man Utd for ANDRE ONANA… despite goalie already making loan transfer
Sports.content:
QUINTON FORTUNE has told Chelsea to raid Manchester United for flop goalkeeper Andre Onana.

The stopper has already left Old Trafford this summer on a loan move to rejoin Turkish outfit Trabzonspor.



Onana, 30, spent last season on loan at the Super Lig outfit and made 33 appearances in all competitions.

The Cameroonian goalkeeper managed just six clean sheets and was unable to convince United of giving him another chance.



His move to Trabzonspor is a straight loan without an option to buy with his contract at United set to expire in June 2028.

Despite this, Fortune still believes that the former Ajax and Inter Milan star would be a useful addition to a club such as Chelsea.



Speaking to Premier Bet, he said: “Andre Onana could be an asset to Chelsea, Newcastle United or Aston Villa in the Premier League.

“You can see the quality for playing out from the back as many managers now want with their style of football, he can be your starting point.

“When you’ve got a goalkeeper like Onana who can ping a ball 50, 60 yards to your striker or midfielder and break the lines with his passes, that can make a huge difference, and he’s one of the best at it.

“He just needs to find his confidence again now because when a goalkeeper makes a mistake unfortunately the whole world sees it.



“I hope he can get back to his best because when you need a goalkeeper to play out from the back, he can be outstanding.”

If Chelsea were able to convince United into a deal which would see Onana’s loan cancelled then he would have to compete with Robert Sanchez for the no1 spot.

The Blues have already added experience to their ranks this summer with veterans Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson arriving.

Fortune earned a Premier League winners’ medal in 2003 as he helped Manchester United lift the title.

The versatile South African admitted that he would have liked to have seen Welbeck return to Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Stick to Football vs Rest is Football: How Lineker and Neville will lock horns in multi-million pound streaming war
Sports.content:
STICK TO FOOTBALL and The Rest is Football are set to battle it out in a multi-million pound streaming war this season.

Having each launched in 2023, both shows went from strength to strength during the World Cup.



Gary Lineker‘s The Rest is Football streamed daily on Netflix after securing an eye-watering £14million deal and performed well enough to earn a two-year extension up to Euro 2028.

Stick to Football, fronted by Gary Neville, also achieved huge numbers on YouTube during the tournament, landing itself a “multi-million pound” deal with Disney+ for the upcoming campaign in the process.



Jamie Carragher, a regular on Stick to Football, made a cheeky dig at his show’s rival after their initial Netflix deal was announced.

The former Liverpool star said: “The Netflix deal for the podcast that no-one listens to. I don’t know anyone who listens to it.”

Asked if it’s a true rivalry by The Athletic in June, however, Lineker ramped things up by saying: “Podcast-wise, no. We’re so far ahead in terms of the football.

“Theirs is a YouTube show and it does really well on YouTube — it’s not really a podcast. I saw Jamie last week and we had a bit of a laugh about it.”

Both shows feature star-studded panels.

Stick to Football is regularly co-hosted by Neville, Roy Keane and Ian Wright – with Jill Scott, Carragher and Wayne Rooney among their other regulars.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Rooney’s involvement will also increase next season, as a new “Stick to United” show is launched.

The Red Devils’ all-time leading goalscorer will team up with YouTube star Mark Goldbridge for 50 episodes – which will also stream on Disney+.

The Rest is Football, meanwhile, features a more regular panel, with Lineker joined by Micah Richards and Alan Shearer.

During the World Cup they were joined by some star guests, however, including Man Utd star Harry Maguire.



Lineker’s show debuted on August 11, 2023 and has earned a not-to-be-sniffed-at 510,000 YouTube subscribers, despite the presenter himself calling it more of a podcast.

It was said to have reached 140,000 daily views on Netflix during the early days of the World Cup.

And last December Goalhanger, The Rest is Football’s parent company, claimed the show had a remarkable seven million monthly listeners.

Stick to Football, which debuted on September 27, 2023, also boasts huge listener numbers.

The Overlap, which is home to the show, has 1.75m YouTube subscribers.



And earlier this year they claimed to have 38m monthly views on YouTube.

A Disney+ premium subscription to watch the show on that platform costs £14.99 per month in the UK.

Netflix, meanwhile, is £18.99 per month for a premium membership.



Both shows have provided agenda-setting punditry.

And they have also ruffled some feathers.

In 2024, Keane sensationally compared Erling Haaland to a “League Two player” during an appearance on the show.

The comment reached then-Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola, who fired back: “I’m surprised this came from a former player. From journalists, I can understand, never been on the pitch but former players is always a surprise. It’s like the referees when they retire they criticise the referees.

“How difficult is that business for the players? It always surprises me. Their memory disappears quickly.



“The problems the players have, they had. They missed a thousand, million times and they were hurt when they were criticised by the former players.”

Lineker, meanwhile, got himself in hot water during Euro 2024 when he called England’s performance in a 1-1 draw with Denmark “s***”.

The comment led to skipper Harry Kane hitting back, saying: “What ex-players have to realise is that it is very hard not to listen to it now, especially for some players who are not used to it or who are new to the environment.

“I always feel like they have a responsibility. I know they have got to be honest and give their opinion but they also have a responsibility as an ex‑England player that a lot of players looked up to.

“People do care about what they say and people do listen to them.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Following post-World Cup breaks, both shows are set to return later this month.

And both, no doubt, will only further grow as agenda-setting football programmes.

Sports.title: The £250m Premier League triple transfer that could cause chaos this weekend
Sports.content:
The £250m Premier League triple transfer that could cause chaos this weekend

Manchester City could be at the centre of £250m worth of transfer dealings before the weeks is out which could see a club-record bid lodged for Chelsea's Enzo Maresca

View 3 Images Rodri could choose to call time on his Man City career this summer (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Manchester City could be involved in three deals this weekend should the blocks fall into place - which could end with them lodging a club-record bid for Enzo Fernandez.

‌



Those at the Etihad are embarking on a new era following the departure of Pep Guardiola and the Enzo Maresca tenure could begin with some wholesale changes to the club's midfield.

‌



Since winning the World Cup, Rodri has been linked with a return to Spain and Barcelona look to have leapt ahead of Real Madrid in the queue, despite their long-term interest. The Catalans have already seen one bid rejected by the Premier League side.

‌



City could ultimately be forced into a corner regarding Rodri, who was a talisman of the Guardiola era and one of the men who drove their winning mentality. He's entered the final year of his deal and returning home is ultimately on his agenda.

Chelsea set Man City strict deadline to complete £120m Enzo Fernandez transfer READ MORE :

Elliot Anderson backs himself to replace Rodri as he doubles down on Man Utd snub READ MORE :

The Manchester outfit are seeking £70m before they consider letting Rodri leave and if Barcelona hit that figure then a move back to La Liga could be on the cards.

The club-record signing of Elliot Anderson, who joined from Nottingham Forest for £116m, is part of planning for life after Rodri with the England star blossoming since leaving Newcastle. Anderson would serve, from a technical point of view, as a similar player to the Spaniard, operating at the base of midfield.

‌



One man from the Guardiola era who was not seen his City career take off has been Tijjani Reijnders. He headed to Manchester from AC Milan off the back of being named the best midfielder in Italy, but the Dutchman found it difficult to nail down regular minutes at the Etihad.

View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez has been linked with a move away from Chelsea this summer (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

He was signed for £46.5m but a move to Saudi Arabia is now on the cards with Al Qadsiah willing to pay £60m. That profit would give City scope to go out and add more quality in the midfield, which would ultimately be needed if Rodri and Reijnders did both depart Manchester. Bernardo Silva also left this summer upon the expiry of his contract.

‌



That comes 12 months after Kevin De Bruyne was allowed to seek a new challenge, heading to Napoli, all of which leaves City undergoing a major revamp of their midfield. Rodri and Bernardo were the last remaining figures of the team that dominated England in the early 2020s.

The club remain in talks with Lille for Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, who enjoyed a stellar World Cup, but Maresca's appointment has led to inevitable links with Fernandez at Chelsea.

View 3 Images Tijjani Reijnders' spell in Manchester could be over inside a year

‌



The Argentina star made noises about leaving Stamford Bridge last season, expressing his desire to live in Madrid, which eventually saw him suspended by the club. New Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso is determine to keep hold of his midfielder, who alongside Moises Caicedo forms one of the more impressive partnerships in the country.

Chelsea want to avoid a scenario whereby Fernandez's future is still being discussed whilst their beginning their Premier League campaign, and as a result have given City until 5pm on Friday to table an offer.

They want £120m for Fernandez, which would exceed the fee City spend on Anderson. The need for midfielders, and the bank balance, may have shifted over the next 48 hours depending on who leaves the blue side of Manchester.

It could all lead to a transfer merry-go-round that sees £250m changing hands if price tags are met with Fernandez becoming one of the most expensive domestic deals ever.

Sports.title: Who is Brian Madjo? The Aston Villa wonderkid tipped to be England's Harry Kane successor
Sports.content:
One game, one goal. That's all it takes for a young striker to put themselves on the list of potential Harry Kane successors, such is the concern among England fans over who'll lead the line once their captain's powers wane.

A despondent Kane admitted in the aftermath of England's heartbreaking defeat to Argentina last month that he doesn't know if he'll play at the next World Cup in 2030. By then, he'll be 36 and likely not the force he was in North America.

That's why England need to start the search for his successor. Step forward: Brian Madjo.

At 17 years and six months old, starting a match of UEFA Super Cup's magnitude is enough to get people talking. But his emphatic first-time finish against European champions Paris Saint-Germain has sparked feverish excitement at Villa Park.

‌



The Aston Villa wonderkid - we can safely label him that now - held off Willian Pacho with relative ease at the back post before firing past Matvey Safonov with his weaker left foot. Although it wouldn't send Villa on their way to victory, it was a goal that announced himself on the European stage.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

EFL 2026-27 predictions with Championship winners decided as West Ham and Wolves discover fate READ MORE :

But talent spotters have known about him for years. Born in Enfield, north London, Madjo moved to Luxembourg with his Cameroonian parents at a young age. His dad, Guy, was a striker himself and played for several EFL clubs.

After playing in the academies of Luxembourgish sides Marisca Mersch and Racing Union, French club Metz - then in the top flight - came calling in 2023. He made his debut last season aged 16 and played a further four games for their first team in the first half of the 2025-26 campaign.

‌



Meanwhile, Madjo won three caps for Luxembourg at senior level. But thanks to FIFA's rules on player allegiance, he was able to switch to England, as those caps had come in friendlies.

Madjo has since played nine times for England's under-17s, scoring four goals and providing one assist. At club level, however, his move to Aston Villa wasn't as simple.

Is Brain Madjo the next big thing? Have your say in the comments section.

5 View 5 Images Brian Madjo scored on his Aston Villa debut in the UEFA Super Cup (Image: Aston Villa/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images) 5 View 5 Images He's already being tipped as a long-term replacement for Harry Kane (Image: Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)

‌



Signed for £10million in January, Madjo initially couldn't play in competitive fixtures due to FIFA's rules on the international transfers of minors. The 17-year-old's transfer was considered an international one due to his appearances for Luxembourg, whereas Villa argued that he was English - given that he was born there and is a UK citizen.

The Premier League club took the dispute to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) and won their legal battle earlier this month. That allowed Madjo to be involved in Wednesday's Super Cup in Salzburg and Unai Emery gave him the nod in the absence of Ollie Watkins.

Afforded extra time off after being part of England's squad at the World Cup, Watkins suddenly faces a fight to be in Emery's first-choice starting line-up. At 30, though, Watkins will still fancy his chances of being Kane's successor himself.

View 5 Images Brian Madjo has enjoyed an impressive pre-season with Aston Villa (Image: Dan Istitene/Getty Images)

‌



Yet his situation at Villa Park could soon be replicated with England. Former Villa striker Stan Collymore reckons that a senior call-up isn't far away. "I guarantee he'll be fast tracked into U21s then seniors by the end of the season," Collymore posted on X during Wednesday's clash.

"England are struggling for strikers, out and out No.9s. We aren't producing them at any senior or youth level. So Madjo (he's raw but his physical dominance of two world class central defenders WILL warrant a look by England scouting analysis) potentially being fast tracked simply addresses a problem.

"Is he good enough? God knows. Is one friendly judgement overkill (he's been very good in pre season and one of Europe's best managers deemed him ready enough to play against the European Champions), no I don't think so. There's a gap in England and looking at him is just common sense."

View 5 Images Brian Madjo has switched his allegiance to England from Luxembourg (Image: Frederic Scheidemann - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



After full-time, Villa right-back Matty Cash was asked about Madjo and described his team-mate as a 'beast'. "All pre-season he's put his body around, scored goals," Cash explained.

"And then tonight he had a few chances as well. He had the header where he probably could've scored and then a good finish. Really happy for him and 17 is still so young. He'll be delighted."

Last year, Luxembourg's technical director, Manuel Cardoni, likened him to Romelu Lukaku - but insists that Madjo can be better. "His profile is similar but, even if we are keeping our feet on the ground, Brian has a more complete profile," Cardoni claimed.

"He is good in tight spaces, really good in terms of positional play. He is also good in terms of going in behind, and he can also feed the ball with both feet. He has huge room for growth."

‌



Plenty of excitement, then. But to offer context for how early we are into Madjo's career, you can't even buy him on Fantasy Premier League yet.

Nevertheless, there'll already be expectation on his shoulders when Villa kick-off their Premier League campaign away to Brighton next Sunday. And with the September-October international break not far away, who knows what Thomas Tuchel is thinking?

Madjo could be rubbing shoulders with Kane sooner than we think - or even breathing down his neck.

‌

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard's call to Virgil van Dijk that saw Liverpool win Man City transfer battle
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard's call to Virgil van Dijk that saw Liverpool win Man City transfer battle

Virgil van Dijk was the subject of a transfer tug-of-war involving Liverpool and Manchester City with a phone call from Steven Gerrard proving key

View 2 Images Liverpool signed Virgil van Dijk despite interest from Man City

Steven Gerrard has recalled a phone call he received from Virgil van Dijk when he was being pursued by Liverpool and Manchester City where he delivered a blunt message to the defender.

‌



Van Dijk had established himself as one of the Premier League's best centre-halves and made it known to Southampton that he wanted to move on. A summer move failed to materialise, but the saga was always going to continue come January.

‌



Liverpool would win the race, spending a then club-record £75million to land Van Dijk, who made an instant impact as he helped the Reds make the Champions League final within months of joining.

‌



Gerrard recalls Van Dijk phoning him to so that he could get a greater impression of the Merseyside outfit. The Dutchman wasn't looking for the Liverpool legend to sell him the club, instead seeking a greater insight, but Gerrard did make it clear that Liverpool's traditions far exceeded City's.

The former midfielder recalled during Captains, a new LFC Original: “He phoned me at the time actually. I knew his agent really well. It was City, Liverpool.

“He said to me, ‘I haven’t phoned you to sort of push me one way or the other, because I know which way you’re going to push me. But just tell me a little bit about Liverpool?’

‌



“I just said to him, ‘Look, if it’s about what the clubs stand for and what the clubs are about, you’re wasting your time because I think you already know the answer to that.’ It was an interesting conversation and I was so happy that he chose us.”

View 2 Images Virgil van Dijk scored on debut for Liverpool back in 2018 (Image: Getty Images)

Van Dijk would enjoy the dream debut, scoring against Everton to knock them out of the FA Cup and concedes he was determined to wear red. “That feeling of, like, I wanted to play for this club so badly, it was so intense," he said. "And the fans embraced me from day one. Scoring also against Everton [on his debut] helped massively too!”

Article continues below

Within 18 months of signing Van Dijk had been named the PFA Player of the Year and proved crucial in Liverpool's Champions League success of 2019. The following year he helped the Reds' end their 30-year wait for a top flight title. Van Dijk remains Liverpool's defensive leader despite turning 35 this summer.

The centre-back, who is also capable of playing at right-back, featured 47 times for Barcelona last season, predominantly on the right side of a back four.

‌



It remains unclear what Arsenal's intentions are for the remainder of the summer transfer window, with speculation of a potential move for a new defender gathering pace amid doubts surrounding William Saliba's return.

Saliba picked up an injury during the World Cup with France and could face up to five months on the sidelines during his recovery, and may even require surgery. Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa is also being monitored.

Jurrien Timber, meanwhile, has been absent from all four of Arsenal's pre-season friendlies so far this summer, and travelled back to England from the club's training base in Spain earlier this month.

The Gunners have emphasised that this decision formed part of Timber's rehabilitation programme rather than a fresh injury setback.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta breaks silence on Myles Lewis-Skelly after Man Utd offered Arsenal star
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta breaks silence on Myles Lewis-Skelly after Man Utd offered Arsenal star

Myles Lewis-Skelly was recently offered to Manchester United, plunging his future at Arsenal into uncertainty with little over two weeks remaining of the summer transfer window

Mikel Arteta praises Myles Lewis-Skelly amid transfer speculation.

Mikel Arteta has refused to rule out selling Arsenal star Myles Lewis-Skelly, saying that he welcomes 'speculation' regarding his players. Lewis-Skelly's future has become a hot topic after he was offered to Manchester United, as Arsenal look to recoup some of the £75million which they spent on new signing Bruno Guimaraes.

‌



Guimaraes' arrival is set to limit game time in midfield for Lewis-Skelly, who United turned down in favour of other targets. That hasn't stopped talk of an exit, although the 19-year-old made his stance clear on Wednesday during a pre-season friendly.

‌



View 2 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly scored for Arsenal in a pre-season friendly (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



Lewis-Skelly scored in Arsenal's 1-1 draw with Como at the Emirates and celebrated by making a heart sign to the crowd before tapping the badge. After full-time, Arteta was asked about Lewis-Skelly's passionate celebration and opted not to put an end to talk of a move away.

"It's good to be emotional after scoring, you should be emotional when you score a goal," the Arsenal boss said. "He's a very emotional player, you see with his gestures on the pitch.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Arsenal reignite Ezri Konsa transfer hopes but face massive Aston Villa problem READ MORE :

Arsenal set to finally break record for transfer sale as bid submitted for Gabriel Martinelli READ MORE :

"I'm not going to talk about speculation. If there is speculation about our players, it's a good sign. That means our players attract attention and are doing a good job."

Chelsea have also been linked with Lewis-Skelly, who signed a new five-year contract with Arsenal last summer. But the Gunners academy product only started five Premier League games last season, with the signing of Piero Hincapie increasing competition for the left-back berth which Lewis-Skelly had made his own earlier in 2025.

He featured in midfield towards the end of the campaign and Arteta has been impressed by his performances over the summer, having played a new role. "He's had a really good pre-season," the Gunners managed added.

‌



"We asked him to play in a different position because he played more as a No.6 - we obviously lacked midfielders from international duty - and I think he had a really consistent pre-season."

Should Arsenal sell Myles Lewis-Skelly? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta didn't shut down the transfer talk (Image: Hayters TV)

‌



Meanwhile, Arteta confirmed that Arsenal aren't finished in the transfer window, which could hasten the club's efforts to offload the likes of Lewis-Skelly. "There is more that we want to do, because every time we have an opportunity to improve the squad and bring more quality and depth, we need to do that," he explained.

"We're actively trying to do so. The thing is in the market, it doesn't just depend on you, and we're very clear on that.

"The will and the desire of the club is unquestionable, but we cannot promise that we're going to do it because it doesn't only depend on us."

Sports.title: EFL 2026-27 predictions with Championship winners decided as West Ham and Wolves discover fate
Sports.content:
Forgive me for going full Jamie O'Hara here, but it's time to rejoice: proper football is BACK.

Yes, last week's Carabao Cup games - and the World Cup - were a nice little distraction to tide us over but the real stuff is back this weekend. And there's plenty of talking points to get stuck into before we prepare to embark on the white-knuckle ride that is a 46 game EFL season.

In the Championship, it's the land of the fallen giants with West Ham, Wolves and Burnley dropping back into the second tier. Will they make an instant return? Or can the teams who narrowly missed out on promotion last year, such as Middlesbrough, Millwall and Southampton, beat them to the post? Don't forget, the top eight will make up the play-offs this year.

Then in League One, Leicester City are the big scalp after dropping into arguably the most unpredictable division of all. They will vie with Sheffield Wednesday and Jack Wilshere's Luton Town for promotion. And in League Two, can Gary Neville and David Beckham's Salford City finally get over the line after some eye-catching transfer business?

‌



Nobody really knows. But Mirror Football's crack team have taken a stab at predicting the big winners and losers...

James Whaling

Championship winners: West Ham

Promoted: Middlesbrough, Wolves

‌



Relegated: Lincoln, Charlton, Blackburn

Top scorer: Raul Jimenez

Surprise package: Portsmouth

League One winners: Leicester

‌



League Two winners: Salford

It's hard to see West Ham not making an immediate return to the top flight. Keeping hold of Jarrod Bowen is an unbelievable bit of business and their squad should be far too strong for the second tier. Middlesbrough look ready to join them in the Premier League after another near-miss last term, somehow managing to lose twice in the playoffs. I fancy Wolves to also bounce straight back, fired by the goals of the returning Raul Jimenez.

At the wrong end of the league, I think Blackburn may sail too close to the sun one too many times and slip into the third division. Charlton look set for another season of struggle and, as well as Lincoln have done reaching the Championship, I think they may find it difficult.

Portsmouth have made some shrewd additions in the transfer window and will be strong at home. Manager John Mousinho has another season of Championship experience under his belt and I think they may surprise a few.

‌



Leicester, similarly to West Ham, have a squad far too strong for the level they are playing at and should bounce straight back to the Championship. Gary Neville, David Beckham and Salford City to win League Two.

View 6 Images Jarrod Bowen and West Ham are the red-hot favourites to win the Championship (Image: Rob Newell/CameraSport)

Ben Husband

Championship winners: Wolves

Promoted: West Ham, Middlesbrough

‌



Relegated: Bolton, Lincoln, Blackburn

Top scorer: Raul Jimenez

Surprise package: QPR

League One winners: Leicester

‌



League Two winners: Salford

I know what you’re thinking…way to go out on a limb. The Championship prediction is made with more than a hint of bias, but I do think if Wolves can get one or two more faces through the door before the window closes they could be formidable. Simply put, a squad including Andre, Kieran Trippier, Raul Jimenez, Mateus Mane and Adam Armstrong should be enough to get it done. Even with some fierce competition from the likes of West Ham, Middlesbrough and Southampton - who will miss out due to their points deduction.

In League One, despite how disastrous his Rangers reign was, Russell Martin is a more than good enough manager to get Leicester back into the Championship. Although they will need to start well to arrest the slide that is now two years in the making.

And in League Two, the arrivals of Macauley Langstaff and Luke Molyneux - to a side that made the play-off final last season - should be enough for Salford City.

‌



Dan Marsh

Championship winners: Wolves

Promoted: Middlesbrough, Norwich

Relegated: Bolton, Charlton, Lincoln

Top scorer: Will Lankshear

‌



Surprise package: Cardiff City

League One winners: Luton Town

League Two winners: Bristol Rovers

Everyone is having West Ham as the bankers to win the league but I'm not convinced Nuno Espirito Santo's pragmatic approach necessarily translates into a top two finish. Their squad is a joke, though, while and they'll be amongst the top teams, clubs will relish the prospect of going to the London Stadium and claiming a major scalp. The scrutiny on West Ham should open the door for Wolves to mount a title challenge with slightly less pressure. They have a manager who has no Championship experience but their squad, too, does not belong at this level and they are my picks for the title. Middlesbrough have levelled up in key areas, namely in goal (Radek Vitek over Sol Brynn) and up front, where Will Lankshear should feast if Boro can repeat the buffet of chances they produced for their forwards last season. I fancy them to finish second with Norwich, resurgent after appointing Philippe Clement midway through the season, a force in the play-offs.

‌



At the other end of the table, Bolton and Charlton have had underwhelming transfer windows. Bolton will be right up against it after coming up through the play-offs, while Charlton, who eventually got over the line last season after winning the previous year's play-offs, have not signed the creative players required for them to 'evolve' as Nathan Jones wishes. Lincoln City have momentum and the nucleus of the squad that destroyed League One last year but losing Michael Skubala and their best player, Jack Moylan, makes an already daunting task even more difficult. Cardiff City are my surprise package tip; I fancy Brian Barry-Murphy's expansive style will translate well to the Championship and star striker Yousef Salech will also handle the step up with aplomb.

Everybody is tipping Leicester to romp League One so I'll go against the curve and tip Luton; they finished the season strongly after winning the EFL Trophy and Jack Wilshere will be all the better for the experience. Salford City have done some eye-catching business and again are heavily fancied to win League Two but Steve Evans has rebuilt Bristol Rovers and I can see them being there or thereabouts under him.

View 6 Images Wolves are likely to be among the teams vying for promotion (Image: David Rogers)

Felix Keith

Championship winners: West Ham

‌



Promoted: Middlesbrough, Norwich City

Relegated: Portsmouth, Cardiff, QPR

Top scorer: Jarrod Bowen

Surprise package: Norwich City

‌



League One winners: Leicester City

League Two winners: Salford City

It really is hard to look past West Ham. Nuno Espirito Santo has been there and done it and, as many have pointed out, Bowen is far too good for the Championship. Something will have to go very wrong for the Hammers to mess it up. Southampton have (so far) managed to hold onto their best players, barring Shea Charles, so should be right in the mix for promotion again. But Tonda Eckert still has an FA charge hanging over his head, which could prompt a lengthy touchline ban. The fallout from Spygate could cost them and help Middlesbrough.

Norwich were a team transformed after Philippe Clement’s arrival last season. They’re only eighth favourites with the bookies for promotion but I can see them surprising a few.

‌



Portsmouth and QPR survived last season but were largely dreadful and could help Lincoln stay up after promotion from League One.

I fancy Russell Martin to get Leicester back up, despite losing some exciting players and the financial might behind the Salford project can’t afford it to stall much longer.

Samuel Meade

Championship winners: West HamPromoted: Middlesbrough, MillwallRelegated: Watford, Bolton, CardiffTop scorer: Jarrod BowenSurprise package: LincolnLeague One winners: LeicesterLeague Two winners: Port Vale The Hammers keeping hold of Nuno Espirito Santo and Jarrod Bowen is their two best bits of business and they'll have too much not to return immediately. Lincoln as a surprise may raise eyebrows, given they won League One with more than 100 points, but plenty have tipped them for the drop.

Leicester are an obvious contender for League One and I'm not convinced by Salford in League Two, despite them being promotion favourites.

‌



View 6 Images New boy Will Lankshear will spearhead Middlesbrough's bid for promotion (Image: Trevor Wilkinson/NurPhoto)

Jeremy Cross

Championship winners: Southampton

Promoted: West Ham, Middlesbrough

Relegated: Watford, Stoke, Charlton

‌



Top scorer: Jarrod Bowen

Surprise package: Millwall

League One winners: Leicester City

League Two winners: Bristol Rovers

‌



Southampton have a lot to prove to the game and themselves this season, following their shameful end to the last one. But getting caught spying on play-off opponents Middlesbrough will give the Saints more than enough fuel to come back fighting again, only this time legally, hopefully. Despite his dubious approach and the subsequent four point deduction, manager Tonda Eckert has done a fine job on the south coast. The season-long loan signing of striker Divin Mubama from Manchester City could prove to be a shrewd move, while the arrival of Lewis Dobbin from Aston Villa in a £10m deal will bring some class and composure to the team.

Middlesbrough have been promotion contenders for a few seasons now, and have only finished outside the top eight once since 2022, so this could well be their time to make a return to the top flight. West Ham, meanwhile, have kept hold of their two best assets despite relegation from the Premier League, in the shape of manager Nuno Santo and England international Jarrod Bowen. Bowen is too good for the Championship, and should be the best player in the entire league this season. If he can maintain the form he's capable of, his goals should give the Hammers an immediate return to the top flight.

Leicester still have the quality to get back into the Championship from League One, while Bristol Rovers look to be the best placed team to win League Two ahead of Salford City.

Brian Dick

Championship winners: West Ham United

‌



Promoted: Middlesbrough, Southampton

Relegated: Lincoln City, Bolton Wanderers, Blackburn Rovers

Top scorer: Jarrod Bowen

Surprise package: Norwich City

‌



League One winners: Leicester City

League Two winners: Barnet

West Ham are the most obvious Championship winners since Newcastle United came down a few years ago. In Nuno they have a proven manager who has won the league before, Jarrod Bowen who will be the best player in the division and a financial muscle and set-up that separates them from the field.

Middlesbrough were the best team in the league for so long last season but ran out of goals, a shortcoming they look to have addressed. Tonda Eckert may have landed in hot water but if he survives any sanction after Spygate, it was clear he had the Saints on the charge last term. Norwich also came like a train after the appointment of Philippe Clement and have recruited well.

‌



Leicester will be too strong not to bounce back from League One, as long as they keep their noses clean on the financial front. Barnet look well-placed to improve on last season’s eighth.

View 6 Images Russell Martin will lead Leicester City in League One (Image: Plumb Images/Leicester City FC)

Peter Smith

Championship winners: West Ham

Promoted: Southampton

‌



Relegated: Lincoln, Bolton, Portsmouth

Top scorer: Taty Castellanos

Surprise package: Stoke City

League One winners: Leicester City

‌



League Two winners: Salford City

The relegated three might have endured varying levels of chaos on their way back to the Championship but their squads should still be strong enough to set the pace. Then again, Southampton had the best squad last year and it took until they changed manager to show it. Even with a points deduction, a couple of key departures and the disdain of their rivals they will be around about it this time.

It is going to be so tight between most of the rest and it will come down to who has a knack of tipping close games in their favour. Stoke’s chances of a good year at last hang on an overhauled midfield. Most seasons since 2018 have all-but finished in January so, with the play-off expansion, it would be a dream for supporters to go into the spring feeling alive.

Leigh Curtis

Championship winners: West Ham

‌



Promoted: Wolves (second), Norwich (playoffs)

Relegated: Portsmouth, Blackburn, Bolton

Top scorer: Jarrod Bowen

Surprise package: Lincoln City

‌



League One winners: Leicester City

League Two winners: Salford City

West Ham's squad is just too good to be at this level for any longer than a season. Keeping Jarrod Bowen was huge and Nuno, despite relegation last season, is still a good and wily manager. I can't see beyond them for the title and I still expect them to strengthen in the transfer market too. It would be a huge shock if they didn't win it. Wolves have made a couple of impressive signings and I fully expect them to be challenging West Ham for the crown. César Peixoto is new to English football, but he looks to have them better organised from what I've seen in pre-season. Plus they aren't finished in the market. As for the playoffs, I was hugely impressed by Norwich last season towards the back end of the campaign. Had a good run under Phillipe Clement. I like the Andre Brooks signing and their forwards are a real handful. I'm predicting them to go up at Wembley. I love Tony Mowbray, but I think he's got his hands full at Blackburn in trying to keep them in the league this season. The signings haven't really caught the eye and there's still problems that need resolving. Portsmouth I thought would go down last year, but they had a decent run towards the back end of the campaign that got them out of trouble, but I think this might be the year. And Bolton I think could be in danger purely because the first season out of League One is always tough because the leap from that to the Championship is vast.

View 6 Images Former Millwall man Macaulay Langstaff will lead the line for League Two promotion hopefuls Salford City this season (Image: Harriet Massey)

‌



Lincoln may well surprise a few people this year. They have a unique way of playing, but they are well organised, their excellent at set-pieces and their pressing is very good. In Ben House they have an absolute machine who never stops running. Sincil Bank is not the easiest place to visit either.

Top scorer is a tough one to call but I am going to say Jarrod Bowen, although I think Mohamed Toure at Norwich and Adam Armstrong at Wolves will run him very close.

In League One, I just think Leicester will be too strong for the division really. Once they get acclimatised the division, they should bounce back straight back. Salford have had an excellent summer of recruitment in the division below and Macualey Langstaff will score bundles at that level. Unbelievable signing for the level.

Tom Coleman

Championship winners: West Ham

‌



Promoted: Wolves, Middlesbrough

Relegated: Lincoln, Charlton, Blackburn

Top scorer: Jarrod Bowen

Surprise package: Swansea City

‌



League One winners: Leicester City

League Two winners: Salford

West Ham have to be favourites to go back up to the Premier League as champions. They've got such a strong squad for this level and I strongly suspect Jarrod Bowen will tear up the division and score loads of goals. Last season's Golden Boot winner Zan Vipotnik will also hope to be in the mix. Middlesbrough really impressed me under Kim Hellberg and I suspect they'll be an even better prospect this time around. Wolves also look to be firmly in the hunt.

At the other end, I think Lincoln will find the step up just a bit too much, but I think Cardiff City and Bolton might just have enough for some reason. Charlton and Blackburn just about escaped last time out but I think they might just struggle this time around.

‌



As for the surprise package, I really like what Swansea have done this summer. They've strengthened in key areas and if they can keep hold of Vipotnik they'll have three top forwards for this level with Adam Idah and Ross Stewart also on the books. I wouldn't be at all surprised if they're part of the play-off conversation.

Nathan Ridley

Championship winners: Middlesbrough

Promoted: West Ham, WolvesRelegated: Lincoln, Charlton, PrestonTop scorer: Jarrod BowenSurprise package: NorwichLeague One winners: LeicesterLeague Two winners: Chesterfield

I can't see any spying from stopping Middlesbrough this year, with Kim Hellberg having made quality additions in key areas over the summer. I'm then backing West Ham to finish second with their stacked squad - hence my pick for top scorer, Jarrod Bowen - and Wolves to win the play-offs.

‌



Going down, I don't see Lincoln's managerial setup working while I think Charlton and Preston's boardroom uncertainty will permeate onto the pitch. Norwich, meanwhile, are almost in danger of the dark horse curse given the amount of fans and pundits tipping them for a play-off finish.

In League One, I can't look past Leicester. And I'll go with Chesterfield for the League Two title - it genuinely would've been York had they not sacked Stuart Maynard.

Sports.title: Atherton: 'England must become Root's team - he has a unique opportunity'
Sports.content:
Fresh from exclusively speaking to Joe Root following his reappointment as England captain, Sky Sports Cricket's Michael Atherton looks further into the move...

Sitting down with Joe Root, he seemed pretty relaxed, optimistic and excited about taking on the captaincy for a second time.

And there's a fundamental reason for that, I suppose. How many of us in life get a second chance at something?

When you're made captain or you lead an organisation, people always say: 'Make sure you do it your way and don't have any regrets at the end of it because you won't get another go at this.'

Joe Root is getting another go at it.

The key points from Joe Root's interview Root rules out curfew despite ECB guidelines and tells players to "be adults" when using alcohol

The England captain was "gutted" at the departure of former England Test head coach McCullum departure but has reasserted his excitement for a new era with incoming coach Stephen Fleming, who he admires

Root admits to "over-bowling" Jofra Archer during his first spell as captain but has vowed to protect England's "generational talent" this time around

Root has refused to rule out a return for Ben Stokes for the 2027 Ashes
