Published 08/13/2026 Published August 13, 2026 Tata Trusts begins search for successor to Tata Sons Chairman Chandrasekaran

India's Tata Trusts said it will set up a selection panel to recommend the next chairman of Tata Sons, the holding company of the $180 billion Tata Group.

The decision follows Chairman N Chandrasekaran's announcement that he will not seek reappointment when his term ends in February.

Tata Trusts praised Chandrasekaran's leadership over the past decade and said a committee would be formed as soon as possible.

The conglomerate has faced a year of leadership tensions and boardroom disputes, including concerns about losses at some group companies.

Chandrasekaran said he was stepping down because of a lack of support from one board member. Indian media reports have linked the disagreement to Noel Tata, head of Tata Trusts.

The trusts own 66% of Tata Sons, giving the charitable institutions significant influence over the future direction of India's largest business group.

World.title: Colombia earthquake: Rescue operation enters 'final phase'
World.content:
Rescuers are racing against a critical 72-hour window to find survivors after a magnitude 7.4 earthquake that has killed 265 people, left hundreds missing, and displaced tens of thousands across western Colombia.

Rescuers worked through a third straight night with time ticking towards the 72-hour mark since a powerful earthquake hit Colombia. That's the period aid agencies consider most critical for finding survivors alive, though it can stretch longer if trapped people have access to food and water.

"We're entering the final phase," Cali Mayor Alejandro Eder said, adding that survivors could still be found afterward but that the odds grow steadily worse. He said crews were still detecting signs of life beneath the rubble and urged speed: "Every minute is vital."

Rescue workers ask for silence as they search for survivors at the site of collapsed buildings Image: Raul Arboleda/AFP

The latest on the Colombia earthquake

The death toll from the quake has climbed to 265, President Abelardo de la Espriella said Wednesday.

De la Espriella said roughly 3,500 people have been injured and nearly 500 remain unaccounted for, though a crowdsourced tracking site used by families put the number of missing far higher, at more than 4,100. More than 25,800 families have been affected in total, he said.

The magnitude 7.4 quake — the strongest to hit Colombia in decades — struck on Monday morning near San Jose del Palmar in the northwestern Choco region. It tore through cities across western Colombia, with Cali and Pereira among the hardest hit, along with Manizales and Quibdo.

In Cali, volunteer rescuer Johana Sanchez described teams pausing every 30 minutes to listen for survivors. "So far, three people have been pulled out alive and three dead," she told AFP.

Officials say 140 buildings collapsed entirely and thousands of homes were damaged or destroyed.

Families grapple with human toll

In Palmira, Santiago Lloreda told Reuters the quake killed his mother and his 13-month-old daughter, Salma, who was too young to have fingerprints on file and would need to be identified through DNA testing. He described his mother as the family's caretaker, saying she "gave everything up to look after the baby."

A man who only gave the news agency his first name, Ricardo, traveled from Miami to recover his sister's body and said his niece was awaiting surgery for a fractured skull, jaw and leg, and a collapsed lung: "She's alive. We know she's going to get better."

Colombia races against time after worst quake in a decade To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Thousands have been left homeless, with many sleeping outdoors in parks or emergency shelters set up in schools and sports arenas, either because their homes were destroyed or out of fear of aftershocks.

Colombia's geological service has recorded 130 aftershocks since Monday's quake.

International aid set to pour in

Response efforts have been especially difficult in Choco, the quake's epicenter, a remote and impoverished region already strained by decades of conflict and displacement. Additionally, lost cell service has made it hard to assess damage in communities reachable only by river.

"This earthquake compounds an already severe humanitarian situation, and there is a need for increased support for the humanitarian response," said Giovanni Rizzo, Colombia director for the Norwegian Refugee Council.

And UN resident coordinator María Jose Torres said in a statement Tuesday that aid groups already working in the region on an earlier peace effort were able to pivot quickly to disaster relief.

The United States has pledged more than $15 million and sent response teams. Mexico has sent military aircraft carrying nearly 20 tons of food along with security personnel, with more aid and rescue specialists on standby. El Salvador's president offered two planes carrying 100 tons of supplies, and a search-and-rescue team from Mexico said it arrived directly from Venezuela, which faced its own major earthquakes in June.

Quake response provides test for new Colombian president

De la Espriella, inaugurated just three days before the earthquake struck, declared an economic emergency and three days of national mourning, and pledged to establish a fund to rebuild hospitals, schools, homes and infrastructure.

"This is undoubtedly a tragedy of immense proportions," he said. "Our efforts are focused on those who remain missing." He has not yet detailed what the economic emergency measures will involve.

Notably, de la Espriella won office on a platform of reduced public spending and a tougher security approach. Analyst Tiziano Breda, of the conflict-monitoring group ACLED, told Reuters that de la Espriella had campaigned in part on cutting funding to the country's disaster-response agency — the same unit now leading the emergency effort.

Experts have cautioned that more seismic activity is possible, if not imminent. "Let's remember that Colombia is full of active fault lines," Rodrigo Leon Loya, a seismologist at the University of the Andes, told AP. "The question isn't whether it can happen again. The question is rather when an earthquake of similar magnitude will occur at another of Colombia’s seismic sources," he warned.

Edited by: Rob Turner

World.title: El turismo, la fábrica de oportunidades de España
World.content:
Con cerca de 700.000 empresas y un récord de visitantes en el horizonte, el sector de los viajes, el alojamiento y el ocio premia a los emprendedores que se especializan en un nicho del mercado, buscan soluciones digitales o convierten la sostenibilidad en una ventaja competitiva

Si hay una industria proclive al emprendimiento ahora mismo en España, esa es la del turismo. Este boyante sector, uno de los principales motores económicos nacionales, no para de batir sus propias cifras. Este año se prevé que se acerque a los 100 millones de visitantes —después de alcanzar los 96,8 millones en 2025—, algo nunca visto en el segundo país más visitado del mundo, solo por detrás de Francia. Y ese volumen inédito, explica David Hernández, fundador de la agencia de viajes personalizados Pangea, genera oportunidades de negocio en toda la cadena de valor: desde los alojamientos a la restauración, el ocio y el transporte.

Triunfar en el sector, asegura Asier Baquero, director del máster en Innovación en Turismo de la Universidad Internacional de La Rioja (UNIR), requiere, no obstante, de estrategia. “Hoy no basta con montar un hotel y esperar a que lleguen los huéspedes; el crecimiento también ha multiplicado la competitividad, por lo que resulta esencial diferenciarse para destacar”, explica el experto. Algo que se consigue a través de la adopción de soluciones innovadoras, de la especialización o de la atención a la creciente sensibilidad de los visitantes por la sostenibilidad.

Consejo de empresario Para emprender hay que ser optimista, pero si te pasas de la raya, te puedes llevar sorpresas David Hernández, Fundador de la agencia de viajes personalizados Pangea

Digitalización para abrirse camino en el mercado

Las soluciones digitales se han convertido en una palanca de diferenciación en el sector del turismo. Hoy la mayoría de las empresas de éxito nacen en el ecosistema de start-ups para ofrecer soluciones directamente al consumidor. Es el caso de la barcelonesa ByHours, que comercializa habitaciones por horas en hoteles de todo el mundo, o el de la madrileña Civitatis, que ha revolucionado el mercado de las actividades turísticas en español al programar visitas guiadas y excursiones por ciudades de Europa, Latinoamérica, Estados Unidos y Asia. “Ambas han identificado una necesidad del turista y han aportado una solución digital que, además, se puede exportar a cualquier parte del globo”, puntualiza Baquero, que da una pista de por dónde puede ir el emprendimiento: “El objetivo de España ya no es atraer más a turistas, sino gestionar de manera más eficiente la estancia de los que visitan el país”.

Otras empresas de ese ecosistema digital, explica Baquero, se crean con el objetivo de brindar soluciones a las grandes agencias de viajes o a las cadenas hoteleras. “Así sucede con los asistentes de inteligencia artificial para centralitas que gestionan las llamadas de los hoteles y las conectan con las reservas, algo que les permite ahorrar muchos recursos”, explica Baquero.

Jugar la baza de la especialización y la sostenibilidad

Encontrar una solución para un grupo concreto de consumidores es otra de las maneras de empezar con buen pie en el sector. Baquero afirma que hoy los hoteles o las agencias de viaje necesitan un apellido: “Un hotel burbuja, una agencia de viajes de lujo o para el segmento LGTBIQ+...”, ejemplifica el experto. Esta es una de las razones que explica el éxito de Nomading Camp, una empresa especializada en alojamientos de lujo en entornos naturales, con propuestas como suites y habitaciones burbuja en cinco destinos, desde los Pirineos hasta la sierra malagueña de Ronda. Lo justifica su fundador, Miquel Vila: “En nuestro caso, la experiencia es muy importante. No ofrecemos solo una cama, sino una noche en pleno bosque con todas las comodidades. La propia habitación es la experiencia. Nuestros clientes no nos escogen porque quieren ir a un destino y necesitan un sitio para dormir, sino que primero escogen nuestra experiencia y luego se desplazan hasta donde van a vivirla”, describe el empresario.

Emprender en el turismo tiene una dificultad añadida frente a otros sectores: no se venden productos, sino experiencias. Un fabricante puede controlar casi todas las características de lo que produce, pero una empresa turística depende de multitud de factores que determinan cómo recordará el cliente su viaje: la atención, el clima, las expectativas del viajero, la coordinación entre distintos servicios... Por eso, el éxito no consiste solo en ofrecer un buen servicio, sino en conseguir que el visitante viva una experiencia que merezca la pena recomendar, defiende Hernández, de Pangea. “Vendemos viajes a destinos cercanos, pero también a 10.000 kilómetros de distancia, con 20 proveedores, por lo que hay una alta probabilidad de que algo salga mal”, destaca.

Consejo de empresario Sigue tu propio camino sin fijarte en el camino de otros emprendedores Miquel Vila, fundador de los alojamientos de lujo en plena naturaleza Nomading Camp

La sostenibilidad gana cada vez más peso como ventaja en esta industria, asegura Baquero. Porque no solo responde a una creciente demanda de los viajeros, sino que también contribuye a reducir costes, acceder a financiación y cumplir la normativa. Por eso cada vez más compañías deciden que su propuesta de valor esté claramente ligada a la sostenibilidad, la economía circular o la conservación del entorno. La catalana Turismo Vivencial se ha hecho un hueco en el mercado ofreciendo consultoría sobre ecoturismo, el turismo respetuoso con el medio ambiente, y organiza actividades que contribuyen a conservar el patrimonio natural y cultural, así como generar beneficios a las comunidades locales. Cada vez son más comunes las compañías que ayudan a negocios del sector a medir su impacto ambiental, como la valenciana Bioscore Sustainability y la madrileña GreeMKO, que no es exclusiva del sector turístico, pero desarrolla programas para la gestión ambiental y el cálculo automatizado de la huella de carbono de hoteles.

Lecciones de los emprendedores

David Hernández y Miquel Vila, que protagonizan el último capítulo de El poder de las empresas, el pódcast de los que hacen , de Banco Sabadell, comparten algunas de las lecciones que han aprendido después de emprender y que pueden ser de utilidad para los empresarios de hoy y mañana. Vila, de Nomading Camp, asegura que, con el tiempo y la distancia, le hubiera gustado compararse menos con otros emprendedores y haber hecho caso a su instinto más frecuentemente: “Merece la pena seguir tu propio camino. Por ejemplo, si tus competidores están haciendo rondas de inversión y tú sientes que no necesitas una nueva, no la hagas; tu gran meta ha de ser que tu negocio funcione, no la ronda en sí misma”. Hernández, de Pangea, señala una actitud como clave a la hora de enfrentarse a cualquier decisión: “No hay que ser demasiado optimista. Me explico: creo que para ser emprendedor es imprescindible ser optimista, pero si te pasas de la raya luego te puedes llevar sorpresas”.

World.title: El BBVA “sigue adelante” tras el fracaso de la opa y la acción se dispara un 60% en 10 meses
World.content:
Los analistas de mercado coinciden en que el banco vasco se revaloriza en Bolsa gracias a la fuerte remuneración a los accionistas y a la solidez de los negocios

Siempre es difícil seguir adelante tras un gran fracaso, incluso cuando se está entre las personas más poderosas de España. En esa situación se encontraba Carlos Torres después de que, el 16 de octubre, los accionistas del Sabadell rechazaran la opa hostil del BBVA. Un portazo a una propuesta de 19.500 millones de euros y a meses de negociaciones y campaña, todo ello un proyecto personal de Torres. En su primera aparición tras la derrota, insistió en que no dimitiría. Además, repitió varias veces una frase en aquellos días de resaca moral: “Vamos a seguir adelante”. Así ha sido y, 10 meses más tarde, la acción del banco vasco acumula un alza del 57%, una de sus mejores rachas desde la pandemia, hasta rozar los 25 euros.

Más información El Santander acelera en banca privada y supera los 300.000 clientes por primera vez

Torres ha abierto el grifo de par en par para sus inversores, con unas operaciones multimillonarias de reparto de dividendos y de recompra de acciones que han disparado al banco en Bolsa. La estrategia tomó forma en julio pasado, cuando el BBVA estimó que podría repartir unos 36.000 millones de euros hasta 2028, en su gran mayoría vía dividendos. El objetivo era estimular a los socios del Sabadell a canjear sus títulos por los del banco vasco. Luego, apenas cinco minutos después de conocerse el fracaso de la opa, Torres ratificó y amplió esa política al agradecer a sus accionistas su “respaldo constante”. Desde entonces, ya se han abonado dos dividendos y se han ejecutado recompras de acciones por 3.960 millones de euros.

El programa de remuneración ha seguido creciendo y, el pasado 30 de julio, el banco vasco anunció una nueva recompra de acciones por otros 2.000 millones de euros, lo que disparó el título un 5% en la sesión. Fue su mejor jornada desde, precisamente, el día en que se conoció el fracaso de la opa y se anunció la aceleración de la remuneración a los inversores. Cinco días más tarde, el BBVA arrebató a Iberdrola el puesto de tercera mayor cotizada española por capitalización bursátil, y desde entonces se queda solo por detrás de Santander e Inditex. Los analistas coinciden en que la política de remuneración ha sido uno de los principales apoyos de la subida de la acción en los últimos 10 meses.

“La recompra habla por sí sola”, señalan los analistas de JP Morgan en un informe del pasado 30 de julio, tras la presentación de los resultados del cierre del semestre. En otro estudio del mismo día, los estrategas de Barclays precisan: “La generación de capital y la remuneración al accionista siguen respaldando la cotización”. Según las estimaciones del banco británico, los dividendos y las recompras de acciones generarán para el BBVA una rentabilidad del 7,9% en 2027, tres décimas por encima de la media prevista para la banca europea.

Si la entidad presidida por Torres puede afrontar estos pagos es porque su negocio marcha bien, y esa fortaleza es, según los analistas, el otro gran motor de su escalada en Bolsa. En la primera mitad de 2026, el BBVA ganó un 11% más que en el mismo periodo del año anterior y alcanzó un nuevo récord de beneficios, con 6.051 millones de euros, impulsado por el crecimiento de los ingresos en sus filiales internacionales y unos menores provisiones.

Además, el banco vasco revisó al alza su previsión de rentabilidad sobre el capital tangible (RoTE) para el cierre del año, uno de los aspectos más destacados por los analistas, hasta situarse en el entorno del 21%, cerca de un punto porcentual por encima de la estimación anterior. “[Los resultados] confirman la buena evolución del negocio y unas perspectivas favorables”, resumen los estrategas de Deutsche Bank en su nota.

Las expectativas pueden ser prometedoras y, como suele ocurrir en Bolsa, también elevan las exigencias de los inversores. Pese al optimismo que ha rodeado al BBVA en estos 10 meses, solo algo más de un tercio de los analistas sigue recomendando comprar la acción, mientras que casi todo el resto aconseja mantenerla, ante el miedo de que el fuerte tirón bursátil pierda fuerza. De hecho, el consenso del mercado recopilado por Bloomberg, que puede cambiar con rapidez de un día para otro, sitúa su precio objetivo un 2,5% por debajo de su precio actual.

La próxima apuesta del BBVA para mantener la racha es adoptar la IA en sus negocios. Como informó este diario a principios de julio, el banco lleva ya tres años formando a sus empleados y, en los últimos doce meses, ha estado desarrollando ocho robots específicos para distintas áreas, desde uno para atender a los clientes en la aplicación hasta asistentes para los banqueros y los analistas de riesgo.

La incertidumbre es una constante en el mundo de los negocios y, en pleno proceso de transformación del BBVA, Torres ha aprovechado para acometer una profunda remodelación de la cúpula del banco. Comunicada en julio a la Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV), la reorganización supuso la salida de ocho de los 23 miembros de la alta dirección. No todos siguen adelante.

World.title: 16 pueblos españoles que piden manga larga cuando cae la tarde
World.content:
Vielha (Lleida). La gran baza de los pueblos seleccionados radica, sobre todo, en la posibilidad de tener que taparse para descansar, algo que se ha convertido en todo un lujo durante la canícula. Es un requisito que cumple Vielha, a la vera de los ríos Garona y Nere, con su casco histórico construido a la manera aranesa, a golpe de piedra, pizarra y madera. Sus mínimas descenderán hasta los 12ºC la noche del domingo; las máximas alcanzarán picos de 33ºC en las horas centrales del jueves y viernes, pero bajarán a los 24ºC (y con probabilidad de lluvias) el lunes, según la Aemet. La capital del Valle de Arán se presenta como un buen campamento base para conocer este territorio del Pirineo catalán, con sus 33 núcleos de población, sus algo más de 10.000 habitantes y sus iglesias románicas. Es recomendable acercarse a la cascada Saut deth Pish, probablemente la más bonita de la zona. Más información: visitvaldaran.com/descubre-la-val-daran/pueblos/vielha/.

World.title: Man admits bomb attack on D66 office, calls it protest
World.content:
The man who set off a firework bomb at the D66 headquarters in The Hague in May has admitted the attack, telling a court it was a protest against Dutch asylum policy and what he called the dismantling of the country.

The 37-year-old, identified as Berry van D., appeared at a preliminary hearing at The Hague district court on Thursday. He is accused of causing an explosion with terrorist intent.

About 30 people, most of them members of the party’s youth wing, were inside the building when the firework bomb went off shortly after 9pm. No one was hurt.

Van D. said he had not known anyone was there because he had seen no lights on and that he never intended to hurt anyone.

Prosecutors said he acted alone and told the court he had a political message and wanted to silence people who think differently, ANP reported.

Van D. was arrested about an hour after the blast in the Grote Marktstraat, the city’s main shopping street, carrying two knives. NOS reported that he has a previous conviction for setting fire to city buses in Tilburg, where he had worked as a driver.

He told the court he had turned to violence because voting and peaceful demonstration had achieved nothing.

Psychiatric assessment

Thursday’s hearing was procedural and no trial date has been set yet. Van D. will be transferred to a forensic psychiatric clinic to assess whether he can be held responsible for his actions.

NOS reported that Van D. presents himself on social media as a supporter of the anti-immigration PVV, and described D66 leader Rob Jetten being sworn in as prime minister in February as a black day for the country.

The office on the Lange Houtstraat was also attacked in September last year, when rioters from an anti-immigration demonstration smashed its windows.

World.content:

One person has been killed and several others injured in an explosion at a site in the Port of Rotterdam, police say.

The blast happened shortly after midday on Thursday at a company on the Moezelweg in Europoort, regional broadcaster Rijnmond reported. Police said they had no further information at this stage.

Multiple people were injured and taken to hospital. Six ambulances, a trauma helicopter and fire crews were sent to the scene.

Rijnmond reported that a hired maintenance crew had been working on pipelines at the site and that something may have gone wrong as those pipes were being disconnected.

Traces of an explosion were visible on a storage tank, the broadcaster said.

Earlier on Thursday, a power cut shut down systems at the Esso refinery on the Botlekweg, sending large flames and black smoke over the port as gas lines were emptied. The Rotterdam-Rijnmond safety authority said it had not established whether the incidents were connected.

World.title: Amsterdam researchers find remedy for fatal child brain disease
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Researchers from the Emma Children’s Hospital at Amsterdam UMC have for the first time found a way to treat a rare genetic brain disease found mostly in children – vanishing white matter, or VWM.

According to The Lancet Neurology, which published the findings, VWM is a neurodegenerative disease “with onset mostly in children aged 1–6 years that causes early death and has no effective therapy.” It’s caused by a genetic defect and occurs in 1 in 100,000 people in the Netherlands.

But now the blood pressure drug guanabenz has been found to inhibit the disease.

In a trial at Amsterdam UMC, 33 children from various countries received guanabenz for four years, while the comparison group included 66 children who did not receive it. Children who received the drug stabilised and ended up needing a wheelchair less often and less quickly.

They also lived – as compared to five patients in the comparison group who died.

“We saw that the disappearance of the white matter in the brain slowed down or even stopped,” chief researcher Marjo van der Knaap told broadcaster NOS.

Moving forward, “the disease-modifying effect of guanabenz should be confirmed in a long-term extension study,” wrote the researchers. The drug also needs the approval of the European Medicines Agency to be used as a treatment for VWM.

World.title: Once-in-a-lifetime solar eclipse has Netherlanders over the moon
World.content:
Eclipse mania took over the Netherlands Wednesday night as people flocked to the coast, roofs and open spaces to watch the largest solar eclipse of the past few decades.

“It looks like a moon giving off light,” a woman on the beach in Petten, a village about 60 kilometers northwest of Amsterdam on the North Sea, told broadcaster NOS. “This is truly very special.”

Indeed traffic jams were rampant on the roads to the sea. But weather conditions were perfect for viewing the eclipse, which was broadcast live on NOS. Some of its broadcasters were clearly moved by the phenomenon.

“This is making me a bit emotional,” NOS weatherman Peter Kuipers Munneke said.

Underwhelmed

But others were less enthusiastic.

College student Sophie joined the crowds to watch the eclipse from the Marineterrein in Amsterdam Oost. Originally planning to make glasses out of old photo negatives, her friend managed to get hold of the hard to come by eye protectors in Amstelveen. But after all the effort, she said they were underwhelmed.

“It wasn’t that special,” she told Dutch News. “The moon didn’t even cover the sun fully. It was like 88% covered and all the sudden, everyone clapped and the sun came back. It wasn’t a total eclipse like in Spain, and it didn’t really become dark. But we had fun.”

A solar eclipse occurs when the moon passes between the sun and earth, blocking all or some of the sun’s light and casting a shadow over the earth.

World.title: Drought means less honey this summer as nectar dries up
World.content:
The persistent drought in the Netherlands has now affected beekeepers, who have noticed that honey production is down this summer. Flowers are blooming for a shorter period, if at all, making it impossible for honeybees to collect the nectar they need to survive.

Professional beekeeper and secretary of the Professional Beekeepers’ Association John Hoogendoorn chalks it up to climate change. “There are increasingly longer periods of drought and higher temperatures, which changes the habitat of the bees,” he told broadcaster NOS. “Nature and the rich biodiversity have deteriorated over the years.”

He said the damage is particularly acute on the dry sandy soils in the east of the country, where the heather honey season has only just begun. Beekeepers report seeing dry shrubs and very little purple, flowering heather there.

Beekeeper Frauke Wessel from Haarlemmermeer has also seen the change. “The bees bring in food to keep their colony alive. But we notice that the honeycomb is no longer filled. The queen bee also lays fewer eggs because she does not get enough food,” she told NOS.

Honeybees need nectar to give them energy for flight and other daily colony tasks. They also convert any excess nectar into stored honey to get them through flowerless winters.

Because the honeybees can’t build up their winter supplies this rainless summer, beekeepers like Hoogendoorn are making up for the lack of honey with dissolved sugar. He told NOS that he needs about 15 kilos of sugar per colony this year to substitute for the honey shortage. “That’s more than in previous years.”

Bees are usually active in the country from the end of February until mid-September. “But due to the high temperatures, the bee season lasts longer and starts earlier,” said beekeeper Joris Knoops.

Flies, wasps, mosquitoes and dragonflies are also suffering from the lack of water.

World.title: Your takeaway habit is feeding Dutch inflation, says DNB

Dutch households are spending so much on takeaway meals that it is impacting national inflation, the Dutch central bank DNB has reported.

Delivery meals have nearly doubled as a share of the average shopping basket, from around 1.6% in 2015 to just over 3% today, DNB said on Thursday.

Prices have climbed fast. With more people spending, delivery firms have also passed on higher wage, energy and ingredient costs, and between 2020 and 2023 the category went from adding less than 0.1 percentage point to inflation to a full 0.35 point.

It has since eased back to 0.13 point – but only because prices stopped rising so fast, not because anyone is ordering less, DNB said.

The bank traces consumer habits back to the Covid pandemic, when locked-down households began using ordering apps much more, especially while working from home.

Dutch inflation has sat above the European Central Bank’s 2% target for years, driven mainly by rents and food prices. The pizza and sushi deliveries are now also hitting the figures.

World.title: Monument against violence in youth care system vandalised
World.content:
Just two months after it was unveiled, the national youth care monument (Nationaal Monument Jeugdzorg) commemorating violence against young people in the system was vandalised in Apeldoorn.

“This feels like a new attack,” Naomi van Aggelen told broadcaster NOS. She worked for years on the monument and was herself wrongly sent to live at a youth care institution when she was 12 years old.

“It is a very sad sight,” she said of the monument meant to acknowledge the suffering of young people in care homes. “Actually, [it’s] a denial of that recognition.”

Located in Apeldoorn’s Zuiderpark, the wings of the monument – titled De Erkenning (The Recognition) – were broken off and are now missing while scratches and dents are visible on what remains.

“Who does such a thing? We have no idea,” said Van Aggelen. “We don’t know where the wings are.”

The council has filed a police report and is said to be reviewing if additional security measures are needed.

The monument was commissioned after a 2019 report by De Winter Commission that found since WW2, some 20,000 children were the victims of violence in youth care. The organising foundation calls it a place of reparation, remembrance and “of vigilance: all current forms of violence must also stop.”

The future of the monument is still unclear. “I have no idea if we should leave the work for what it is,” said Van Aggelen. “Maybe we should glue it, then it symbolises another broken child in youth care.”

World.title: Barcelona legend Xavi appointed Netherlands head coach
World.content:
Xavi Hernández has been appointed head coach of the Netherlands men’s national team on a contract running to the 2030 World Cup, the Dutch football association KNVB has announced.

The 46-year-old Spaniard succeeds Ronald Koeman, who stepped down after the Netherlands’ last-32 defeat by Morocco at this summer’s World Cup. His appointment ends a long and closely watched search, and comes as a surprise after several higher-profile names fell away.

Former Feyenoord and Liverpool coach Arne Slot, ex-Ajax and Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag and PSV’s Peter Bosz all ruled themselves out, while the KNVB passed over Jong Oranje coach Michael Reiziger and Louis van Gaal. On

Tuesday, Roberto Martínez was reportedly the front-runner, though the KNVB never held direct talks with him.

“A son of Dutch football”

Xavi becomes the first foreign coach of Oranje since the Austrian Ernst Happel, who led the side to the 1978 World Cup final.

“It is a great honour to become head coach of the Netherlands national team,” he said in a statement released by the KNVB. “As someone who was developed at the FC Barcelona academy, with strong influences from, among others, Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, I feel a special connection to Dutch football. You could say I am, in a way, a son of Dutch football.”

As a player, Xavi is regarded as one of the best midfielders of his generation, winning four Champions League titles in more than 750 games for Barcelona and lifting the 2010 World Cup with Spain – beating the Netherlands in the final – as well as the European Championship in 2008 and 2012.

He started out as a coach at Al Sadd in Qatar, then took charge of Barcelona in 2021 – also succeeding Koeman – and won the Spanish league title in 2023, but made little impression in Europe before leaving in 2024.

Restoring tactics

The KNVB has handed Xavi an explicit task: restore the attacking, possession-based football long associated with the Dutch game, after a World Cup exit widely seen as a low point in style as much as result.

“As a coach, he has been shaped by years of working with top coaches who share a footballing vision that aligns very well with the way we want the Netherlands national team to play,” said the KNVB’s director Nigel de Jong. He pointed to “taking the initiative, playing dominant and attractive football, combined with the flexibility required in modern football at the highest level.”

Xavi said he shared that ambition. “The Netherlands has a rich football culture and a clear vision that strongly appeals to me: attacking football, based on possession, with creativity, passion and conviction,” he said. “The main objective is always to win, but I prefer to do so in a way that reflects those characteristics and that people can enjoy watching.”

He will be presented at the KNVB’s Zeist headquarters on August 25 and takes charge for the first time on September 24, at home to Germany in the Nations League.

Poles are building up wealth at the fastest pace in years, with the combined value of household financial assets surpassing 4 trillion zloty (€930 billion) for the first time, according to new data from the Polish Development Fund (PFR), a state entity. The figure reached 4.1 trillion zloty at the end of the first quarter of this year, up 4.3% from the previous quarter, said PFR. That was the largest quarterly increase in just over six years. On an annual basis, assets rose 15.3%, the fastest pace in five years. After deducting liabilities, household net financial assets stood at 3.2 trillion zloty, also a record. Net assets were up 18.4% from a year earlier and 4.9% from the previous quarter. Ponad 4,1 bln zł – tyle wynoszą już aktywa finansowe polskich gospodarstw domowych. To historyczny rekord. W najnowszej analizie PFR pokazujemy, że w ciągu roku wzrosły o 15,3% – to jedna z najwyższych dynamik w historii. Skala i tempo wzrostu aktywów pokazują też, jak duży jest… pic.twitter.com/fSx1yOZtkn — Mikołaj Raczyński (@MikRaczynski) August 7, 2026 The biggest contribution to the quarterly increase came from what PFR classifies as “other equity holdings”, which include shares in limited liability companies, partnerships, cooperatives and mutual insurance societies. They rose by 61.5 billion zloty. Bank deposits recorded the second-largest increase (44.4 billion zloty). Despite the strong rise in equity holdings, bank deposits and cash remained the largest components of household financial assets, accounting for 26.3% and 11.1% respectively. Pension and disability funds accounted for 10.5% of household financial assets. Meanwhile, shares listed on stock exchanges and regulated over-the-counter markets made up 2.9% of household financial assets. Their value is equivalent to 3% of GDP, one of the lowest shares in the European Union, where the average is 8.2%. Although shares make up only a small share of household assets, the Polish stock market has performed strongly in recent years, with its blue-chip index reaching a record high last week and breaking its previous high set 19 years ago. By contrast, Polish households have a relatively high level of cash holdings. Cash was equivalent to 11.5% of Poland’s GDP in the first quarter, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). PFR’s data also show that household liabilities in Poland increased by 5.2% year-on-year to more than 891 billion zloty in the first quarter, well below the rate of asset growth. Long-term loans accounted for 92.2% of liabilities, while short-term loans accounted for 5.1%. Rising household wealth reflects three decades of strong economic growth in Poland, accompanied by a rapid rise in wages and living standards. Earlier this year, state research agency CBOS found that a record 39% of Poles say they are financially comfortable, up from just 3% in the early 1990s. Separate data from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, show that only 2% of the population live in severe deprivation, the lowest level on record. Poland last year rose to its highest-ever level in a measure of household prosperity in European Union member states, overtaking four other countries. That growth has also fuelled a rapid increase in the number of ultra-wealthy people in Poland, whose number has almost doubled since 2019. However, the PFR data show only total combined household assets and liabilities, not how they are distributed across society. The personal data of almost 19 million people, including medical information, has been compromised in a major cyberattack on a company that provides services to thousands of medical facilities in Poland. “We are dealing with one of the largest incidents in Poland’s history,” said digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski on Wednesday. He urged people to use government services to check whether their data is affected and to “lock” their national identity number to prevent potential fraud. (￼🧵 1/2) 💬 Dziś doszło do poważnego wycieku danych w firmie MyDr, który może obejmować blisko 19 milionów osób korzystających z opieki medycznej. W związku z sytuacją krytyczną zostały natychmiast podjęte działania mające zabezpieczyć dane i wyjaśnić okoliczności incydentu –… pic.twitter.com/nIp6EvbKiu — Ministerstwo Cyfryzacji (@CYFRA_GOV_PL) August 12, 2026 The attack targeted MyDr, a company that provides services used by many medical facilities in Poland. Its data includes patients’ personal information, as well as medical details such as diagnoses and prescriptions. It was first reported on Monday by Zaufana Trzecia Strona, an IT security news service, which said that it had been contacted on Saturday by the alleged perpetrators, who claimed to have accessed the data of around 18.8 million people. The hackers, who have not been identified, had also sent a screenshot from the compromised database showing the personal data of “one of the most important politicians in Poland”, added Zaufana Trzecia Strona. Shortly afterwards, MyDr confirmed that it had “become the target of an external, deliberate criminal activity involving some of our data”. In an update on Wednesday, it said that, at the time of writing, there was no evidence that the data had been published anywhere. Największy wyciek danych osobowych w historii Polski i co możemy z nim zrobić – nasza analiza incydentu w MyDr i jego potencjalnych skutków.https://t.co/vXUmVfpPAP Opisujemy aktualny stan wiedzy i możliwe scenariusze rozwoju sytuacji. pic.twitter.com/uqhjz1CjZ1 — ZaufanaTrzeciaStrona @zaufanatrzeciastrona@infosec (@Zaufana3Strona) August 13, 2026 Gawkowski addressed the issue at a press briefing on Wednesday. He noted that “there is no indication we are dealing with an external attack…from Russia or any other country”. Poland has recently regularly been targetted by Russian state-linked hackers. It is “very likely” that cybercriminals are behind the attack on MrDr, said Gawkowski, who pledged that there would be an “uncompromising” response from the Polish security services. The minister advised Poles to check in a secure government database whether their data had been leaked. He also advised citizens to use the state web portal, known as mObywatel, to “lock” their identity number, known as a PESEL, which prevents fraudsters from using it. Around 12,000 medical facilities use MyDr’s services, the digital affairs ministry told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). The company claims that it processes three million medical consultations and 2.7 million prescriptions a month, reports the Gazeta Wyborcza daily. A letter sent to a Polish court by Marcin Romanowski, who served as a deputy justice minister in the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government and is now on the run from criminal charges, suggests that he is residing in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links with Russia. The Polish authorities have been trying to locate and extradite Romanowski, whose whereabouts have been unknown since he fled Budapest earlier this year after Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who had granted him asylum, lost power. Były wiceminister sprawiedliwości ma przebywać w Tyraspolu, stolicy zbuntowanej mołdawskiej prowincji znajdującej się pod patronatem Rosji. Spod tego adresu w Naddniestrzu polityk PiS miał wystąpić o wydanie listu żelaznego.https://t.co/m05dtQv3KV — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) August 12, 2026 On Wednesday, following media reports that Romanowski had sent a letter to the Polish authorities from Transnistria, a spokeswoman for Warsaw’s district court, which is responsible for extradition matters, confirmed to news website Gazeta.pl that this was the case. “The letter and envelope indicate that the package was sent to the court from Tiraspol in Transnistria,” said judge Anna Ptaszek. “It bears his handwritten signature.” Przemysław Nowak, the spokesman for Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office, also confirmed to broadcaster RMF that Romanowski had sent the letter, in which he indicated that he was residing in Tiraspol, the capital of Transnistria, and requested safe passage to Poland. The fugitive politician said that he would be willing to appear in court or before prosecutors, on the condition that he was not placed in detention, said Nowak, who added that prosecutors had not yet taken a position on Romanowski’s request. Transnistria is a region of eastern Moldova, bordering Ukraine, that sought to become a separate state in the early 1990s, even fighting a war between 1990 and 1992. Today, the territory, which has a population of around 360,000, operates as a de facto state but is not recognised by any other country. Transnistria has close ties with Russia, which maintains a military “peacekeeping” force there. The territory’s flag and national emblem feature the Soviet hammer and sickle. Romanowski’s apparent presence in the Russian-linked territory was condemned by figures from Poland’s government. “I would say that Romanowski is now very likely under the influence of Russian intelligence,” said deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk, quoted by broadcaster TVN. Paweł Wojtunik, the former head of Poland’s Central Anticorruption Bureau (CBA), who previously worked in Moldova, wrote that “it is impossible to enter [Transnistria], let alone to live there, without the consent of the local KGB, which is directly managed by the Russian GRU and FSB [intelligence agences]”. – Dzisiaj powiedziałbym, że Romanowski z dużym prawdopodobieństwem jest pod wpływem rosyjskich służb – ocenił wiceszef MON Cezary Tomczyk. Sprawę skomentował też szef MSZ Radosław Sikorski.https://t.co/LuWw0bkh2j — tvn24 (@tvn24) August 12, 2026 Even a deputy leader of Romanowski’s own party, the national-conservative PiS, was unwilling to defend him. In an interview with Polsat News, Przemysław Czarnek noted that it is still not confirmed that Romanowski is in Transnistria. But he agreed, when asked by the host, that it “would be crossing a line” for Romanowski to be in the territory. Romanowski served as a deputy justice minister in the former PiS government between 2019 and 2023. He remains a member of parliament, despite having fled Poland in December 2024 after prosecutors sought to bring charges against him for 11 alleged crimes, including participating in an organised criminal group. Those alleged offences relate to Romanowski’s time at the justice ministry, which was then led by Zbigniew Ziobro, who is also wanted on multiple charges. Both Romanowski and Ziobro obtained asylum in Hungary when the country was led by PiS-ally Orbán. The Polish government says that Hungary has revoked the refugee status and travel documents granted to fugitive ex-justice minister Zbigniew Ziobro by Viktor Orbán. Poland will now seek Ziobro's deportation from the US, where he fled after leaving Hungary https://t.co/TcVw0AiEMX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 2, 2026 However, after Orbán lost power earlier this year, Ziobro fled to the United States, where he remains. Last month, Poland requested his extradition, though that is a process that could take years. Romanowski, meanwhile, disappeared completely, leading to months of speculation as to his whereabouts. Both politicians have denied the allegations against them and have claimed to be victims of “political revenge” by the current government, a more liberal coalition led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk that took power in December 2023. They have argued that they would not be able to receive a fair trial in Poland while Tusk remains in power because of the government’s influence over the judicial system. On Wednesday, Romanowski’s lawyer, Bartosz Lewandowski, confirmed that his client had requested safe passage to Poland and that he was “outside the territory of the European Union”. However, he did not confirm that Romanowski is in Transnistria. Poland has formally asked the US to detain and extradite former justice minister @ZiobroPL, who faces multiple criminal charges. The Polish government has appealed to Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, to reverse its decision to exclude Poland from its European roaming area. It says that Polish users, who will now face greater costs when travelling, should not be treated as “second-tier customers”. Starlink, which provides users with portable terminals that act as receivers for internet connections from its network of satellites, offers a “Roam” service that lets customers continue using their connection outside their home country without extra charges as long as they remain within their designated region. One region is Europe, in which Starlink has included 36 countries and territories. However, the firm makes clear that “Poland is not included in the Europe region”, meaning users registered in that country are not included in the Roam system. The company offered no explanation for Poland’s exclusion from the system. Some media reports have suggested that it is because terminals registered in Poland are used in Ukraine. However, Ukraine is itself not included in Starlink’s European “Roam” region. The company’s decision prompted an angry response from Polish government ministers. “I do not agree with a global technology company treating Poles worse than other Europeans,” wrote digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski on X, the social media platform owned by Musk. “If Elon Musk’s SpaceX wants to operate in Poland, benefit from the Polish market, and earn from Polish customers, it must treat them fairly and on equal terms,” he added. “That is why I have appealed to SpaceX for the urgent restoration of equal terms for the company’s Polish customers.” Nie zgadzam się, żeby globalna firma technologiczna traktowała Polki i Polaków gorzej niż innych Europejczyków. Jeżeli @SpaceX @Elon Musk chce działać w Polsce, korzystać z polskiego rynku i zarabiać na polskich klientach, musi ich traktować uczciwie i na równych zasadach. Od… — Krzysztof Gawkowski (@KGawkowski) August 12, 2026 Meanwhile, foreign minister Radosław Sikorski revived a dispute he had with Musk last year over the provision of Starlink terminals to Ukraine during its war with Russia. The proportion of Poles who hold a negative view of Polish-Ukrainian relations has risen to 46%, the highest figure ever recorded by Polish state research agency CBOS. Only 12% think relations are good. By contrast, three years ago, in mid-2023, only 3% had a negative view and 64% a positive one. Meanwhile, CBOS also found that belief among Poles that reconciliation between the two neighbours, who share a difficult history, is possible is at its lowest level on record, 53%, down from 78% three years ago. The findings follow other polls showing worsening attitudes towards Ukraine and Ukrainians in Poland in recent years, and come amid an ongoing diplomatic crisis triggered by President Volodymyr Zelensky naming a military unit after a group that massacred Poles in World War Two. Przekonanie o możliwości pojednania między Polakami 🇵🇱 a Ukraińcami 🇺🇦 spadło do najniższego poziomu w historii naszych pomiarów. 📙 Więcej w komunikacie #CBOS "Stosunki polsko-ukraińskie" ⤵️ https://t.co/kw2o4upY3Q#Ukraina #Ukraińcy pic.twitter.com/LItCFC3f2m — CBOS (@CBOS_Info) August 11, 2026 Relations between Poland and Ukraine improved significantly in the wake of Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, as Poland welcomed millions of Ukrainian refugees and provided Kyiv with extensive military, humanitarian and diplomatic support. However, since 2023, those relations have been hit by a series of controversies over Ukrainian agricultural exports, border blockades by Polish farmers and truckers, and, above all, over the two nations’ difficult World War Two history. Among Poles who now hold a negative view of relations, CBOS also asked them who was responsible for the situation. A large majority, 65%, primarily blamed Ukraine, while only 4% said it was Poland’s fault and 28% placed responsibility on both sides. In its regular surveys since 1997, the agency has also asked Poles if they believe that reconciliation between Poles and Ukrainians is possible or not. In the early 2000s, that figure rose to a record level of 81%, and in 2023 it still stood at 78%. Now, however, it has dropped to an all-time low of 53%. There have long been tensions between Poland and Ukraine over their difficult, intertwined histories, in particular during the first half of the 20th century. In World War Two, Ukrainian nationalists killed around 100,000 Polish civilians, mostly women and children, in an ethnic-cleansing operation known as the Volhynia massacres. Poland has officially recognised that episode as a genocide. However, Ukraine rejects that label and also points to the persecution of Ukrainians who lived in the interwar Polish state, as well as to massacres of Ukrainians by Polish groups during World War Two. Long-simmering tensions between Poland and Ukraine over WWII massacres have finally boiled over, prompting a diplomatic crisis.@danieltilles1 looks at how we got here and what it may mean for the two countries and Europe more broadly https://t.co/a8tiYJJHRr — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 22, 2026 Those tensions recently boiled over after Zelensky, in May this year, approved a request to rename a military unit after the “heroes of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA)”, the group that led the Volhynia massacres but is remembered positively in Ukraine for its role in fighting Moscow-imposed Soviet rule. Zelensky’s decision prompted his Polish counterpart, Karol Nawrocki, to strip the Ukrainian president of Poland’s highest honour. While tensions have since calmed somewhat, the dispute remains unresolved. However, even before that diplomatic crisis broke out, polling showed increasingly negative attitudes in Poland towards both Ukraine and Ukrainians, who are by far the country’s largest immigrant group. In its annual survey of attitudes towards various national and ethnic groups, published in February, CBOS found that the proportion of Poles who said they disliked Ukrainians had increased by five percentage points year-on-year, to 43%. Only 29% said they liked Ukrainians. In January, CBOS reported that opposition to accepting Ukrainian refugees in Poland had risen to its highest ever level. In December 2024, a poll in Ukraine found that positive sentiment towards Poles had fallen by half in the space of two years. The proportion of Poles opposed to accepting Ukrainian refugees has reached its highest ever level of 46%, up from 3% in the wake of Russia's full-scale invasion. Other recent surveys have also indicated declining sympathy towards Ukrainians among Poles https://t.co/DLPGY2ToZG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 7, 2026 Meanwhile, the number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland rose by 30% in the first half of 2026, including a number of high-profile incidents. Poland’s government has blamed increasing anti-Ukrainian rhetoric from the right-wing and far-right opposition. Last month, Ukraine’s foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, called on “Polish politicians to stop inciting hatred against Ukrainians”. CBOS’s new study shows that attitudes towards relations with Ukraine differ significantly depending on political affiliation. Whereas 35% of supporters of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO), Poland’s main ruling party, hold a negative view of relations, that rises to 52% among voters of the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party and 81% for the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja). Among those with a negative view, 49% of KO voters blamed Poland and Ukraine equally for the situation while 10% blamed mainly Poland. By contrast, 86% of Confederation supporters and 82% of PiS supporters placed responsibility on the Ukrainian side. Demonstrations took place in 25 Polish cities on Sunday against the “growing wave of hate and violence” against Ukrainians, who are Poland’s largest immigrant group. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has unveiled its first frigate to enter service in decades at a ceremony in the Baltic Sea port of Gdynia, where the ship was constructed. The development marks a major milestone in a 15 billion zloty (€3.5 billion) programme to modernise the ageing Polish navy and strengthen NATO’s maritime defences. “Poland is becoming a maritime power in the Baltic Sea,” declared Prime Minister Donald Tusk at a ceremony to name the new ship, which he attended alongside opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki in a rare show of unity. The three frigates are intended to form the core of Poland’s surface fleet and will replace Poland’s two current Oliver Hazard Perry-class frigates, which were constructed in the 1970s and transferred from the US Navy in the years 2000 and 2002. Nawrocki, meanwhile, said that the modernisation of the Polish navy “sends a clear message that we will develop our armed forces in every theatre – on water, on land, and in the air”. World.title: Negative views of Poland’s justice system have grown under Tusk government, finds state pollster
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The proportion of Poles who negatively assess their country’s justice system has increased under the current government, despite its promises to restore the rule of law and ensure that courts function more effectively and independently. New polling by state research agency CBOS found that, in June this year, 61% of Poles had a negative view of the functioning of the justice system, up from 55% in 2022 and 51% in 2017, when the former Law and Justice (PiS) government was in power. Only 26% now positively assess the system, down from 28% in 2022 and 36% in 2017. The last time positive views were lower was in 2005 (22%). The findings come two and a half years after the current government, a coalition ranging from left to centre right led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, came to power in December 2023, replacing the national-conservative PiS administration. One of Tusk’s main promises was to restore the rule of law after eight years in which PiS had implemented a series of contested judicial reforms that experts, European courts and many Polish judges had condemned as undermining the independence and functioning of the judiciary. However, Tusk’s government has struggled to implement its promised changes. In many cases, its efforts have been blocked by PiS-aligned Presidents Andrzej Duda and Karol Nawrocki or other officials appointed under the former government. But in other cases, such as with a pledge to separate the functions of justice minister and prosecutor general, which were fused by PiS in 2016, the current ruling coalition has simply not followed through on its promises. In its latest polling, CBOS found that supporters of the current opposition are most dissatisfied with the functioning of the justice system: 72% of PiS voters have a negative view, as do 71% of those who support the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja). However, even among voters of Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party, a majority, 53%, have a negative opinion, with only 38% holding a positive one. Interestingly, public attitudes towards judges themselves have hardly changed. Currently, 19% of Poles have a positive view towards them and 23% a negative one. That is similar to findings in 2017 (22% positive, 24% negative) and 2012 (19% positive, 23% negative). More Poles (35%) think that the rule of law has got worse under Tusk's government than believe it has improved (24%). A further 28% think there has been no change, finds a new poll https://t.co/KkiuY2vDSW — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 5, 2025 When asked to identify the greatest problems with the justice system, Poles instead often point to structural issues – that is, those that are under the control of politicians. The most commonly identified problem (chosen by 38% of respondents, who could select up to three main problems) was “prolonged proceedings” in court cases. The second biggest issue was “politicisation of courts” (18%). Only 4% said that “judges’ neglect of duty, incompetence and impunity” were among the biggest problems. However, 23% of respondents were unable to name a single major issue that the justice system faces. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 CBOS’s findings echo a number of other polls. After the first year of Tusk’s government, a survey by SW Research for the Rzeczpospolita daily found that 35% of Poles thought the rule-of-law situation had got worse, compared to only 24% who thought it had improved. Another poll by the same agency for Onet, a news website, in January this year similarly found that 40% of Poles believe the justice system has not improved under the current government, while only 33% think it has got better. In response to the latter poll, justice minister Waldemar Żurek admitted to Onet that there had been problems in addressing the rule of law. But he blamed the “hurdles [put] in our path” by Presidents Duda and Nawrocki. Opposition-aligned President @NawrockiKn has vetoed a government bill intended to reform a judicial body at the heart of Poland’s rule-of-law crisis. He argued that the measures would simply create even greater “legal chaos” https://t.co/I7FHRKIoP1 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 19, 2026 In 2024, Duda refused to sign government bills overhauling the Constitutional Tribunal (TK), which still contains judges illegitimately appointed under the former PiS administration. As a result, Tusk’s government refuses to recognise rulings issued by the TK. In February this year, Duda’s successor, Nawrocki, vetoed a government bill intended to restore the legitimacy of the National Council of the Judiciary (KRS), the body responsible for nominating judges to positions on courts. In 2017, the KRS was overhauled under PiS in a manner that rendered it illegitimate, according to multiple Polish and European court rulings. That in turn has led to doubts over the legal status of around 3,000 judges appointed by the KRS since 2017 and all the rulings issued by them. Nawrocki has also refused to swear in four new TK judges nominated by parliament this year, despite an order by the European Court of Human Rights that they be allowed to take up their positions. The European Court of Human Rights has ordered Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) to accept four judges whom opposition-aligned President Nawrocki refused to swear in. World.title: Indians and Colombians now third and fourth largest groups of foreign workers in Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Indians are now the third-largest group of foreign workers in Poland, followed by Colombians, according to new data from the country’s Social Insurance Institute (ZUS). Ukrainians remain by far the largest immigrant group, followed by Belarusians. The figures also show that the overall number of registered foreign workers has risen more than 8% over the last year, a faster rate of growth than in recent years. However, the government official responsible for migration strategy says this is because stricter government measures have pushed some employers to register previously uninsured workers. The ZUS data, reported by Dziennik Gazeta Prawna (DGP), a leading daily, show that there were 1.34 million foreign workers registered in ZUS at the end of June, up from 1.24 million at the same point last year. That 8.2% increase is larger than the growth rate of around 6% seen in each of the previous two years, notes the newspaper. Maciej Duszczyk, the deputy interior minister responsible for migration, commented that the rise actually reflects the government’s tougher migration strategy, which he said “forces employers to report for insurance those who arrived earlier” but were working unregistered The official pointed to recent data showing that, in fact, in the first half of this year, Poland issued 50% fewer work permits to foreigners than in the same period of 2025. Dane ZUS pokazują dokładnie to co zakładaliśmy w Strategi Migracyjnej. Radykalny spadek liczby wydawanych, nowych zezwoleń na pracę (ponad 50% rok do roku) wymusza na pracodawcach zgłaszanie do ubezpieczenia, tych którzy przyjechali wcześniej. Tylko w pełni legalne zatrudnienie! — Maciek Duszczyk (@MaciekDuszczyk) August 11, 2026 Ukrainians remain by far the largest group of registered foreign workers, with 901,000 now in the system, a 10.1% rise from a year earlier. Belarusians (144,000, up 4.9%) remain in second. But two non-European migrant groups whose numbers have been growing rapidly in recent years now occupy third and fourth place: Indians (25,500, up 4.9%) and Colombians (23,000, up 31%, which was the fastest growth of any national group). Georgians, who had previously been the third-largest group, saw their number fall by 17% to 22,000, meaning they are now in fifth, ahead of Filipinos (15,400, down 2%), Moldovans (14,200, down 1%), Nepalis (13,400, up 8.3%), Vietnamese (12,200, up 6.1%), and Russians (11,800, down 2.5%). Latin American migration to Poland is booming, with 45,000 work permits issued last year, five times more than in 2022@Gosia_Tomczak looks at what is driving this trend and what challenges and opportunities it has created for both the migrants and Poland https://t.co/tl1wUTCaC0 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 15, 2025 ZUS’s data also show that foreign workers are increasingly establishing their own businesses in Poland, which Dziennik Gazeta Prawna notes is a sign that they are establishing longer-term ties with the country but also a result of an easier online system for registering businesses. In 2021, only 22,700 foreigners had a registered business in Poland, a figure that now is now almost five times higher, at 102,000. The rise has been driven in particular by Ukrainians, many of whom are legally entitled to establish companies in Poland under the same terms as Polish citizens. As a result, 7.6% of foreign workers now run their own business, up from 6.7% a year ago and from 2.7% before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, which led to a wave of Ukrainian refugees settling in Poland. Ukrainian refugees boosted Poland’s GDP by 2.7% last year while not raising unemployment or lowering wages, finds a report by the UN @Refugees agency and @Deloitte "Whoever thinks refugees are a burden on the economy should think again," says @UNHCRPoland https://t.co/rOvtOvBNwG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 12, 2025 Over the last decade, even before the war in Ukraine, Poland has experienced a wave of migration unprecedented in its history and among the largest anywhere in Europe. For six years running, between 2017 and 2022, it issued more first residence permits to immigrants from outside the European Union than did any other member state. Much of the surge in immigration came during the rule of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government from 2015 to 2023, despite its strong anti-migrant rhetoric. The current government, a more liberal coalition led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, came to power pledging to reduce immigration, which it said had got out of control under PiS. Under Tusk’s government, in 2024, Poland issued the lowest number of residence permits to non-EU immigrants in a decade. In 2025, the government introduced tougher entry requirements for foreign workers and students. It has also stepped up deportations of foreigners who have broken the law. However, Duszczyk notes that the current government still sees “selective and responsible migration” as a way to “maintain the competitiveness of the economy without limiting wage growth”. ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers.
