World.title: Iraq sets September 30 for US-led coalition exit as Al-Zaidi turns focus to Iran-linked militia weapons
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has reaffirmed Sept. 30 as the end date for the US-led coalition’s military mission in Iraq, putting more pressure on Baghdad to confront what could be the most difficult aspect of its sovereignty agenda: bringing weapons held by powerful Iran-aligned factions under state control.

During a meeting with U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) Commander Admiral Brad Cooper, Al-Zaidi said that October 1 will signal the beginning of a “new phase” for Iraq in the absence of a foreign coalition military presence.

The Prime Minister again emphasized the importance of the Iraqi state having exclusive control over weaponry, citing sovereignty, security, and economic growth.

Iraqi authorities said plans are already beginning to hand over remaining coalition locations, notably those in northern Iraq, to Iraqi security forces before the deadline.

The timeline is based on a 2024 agreement between Baghdad and Washington to end the coalition mission and transition the US-Iraq security partnership to direct bilateral cooperation.

However, the departure eliminates one of the primary justifications used by Iran-backed militias to preserve their weapons and strike US objectives.

Several prominent Iran-aligned factions work inside or alongside the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), who are officially part of Iraq’s governmental security system.

The PMF is made up of various groups with varying political and ideological perspectives, and it should not be viewed as a unified bloc.

However, organizations like Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba, and other Iran-aligned militias have maintained strong ties with Tehran and have rejected calls to relinquish their weapons.

Their actions have become an increasingly severe issue for Al-Zaidi’s administration.

Recent strikes ascribed by neighboring governments to Iran-backed forces operating from Iraqi soil have jeopardized Baghdad’s improved ties with Saudi Arabia and other Arab countries, as well as led to foreign military intervention in Iraq.

The escalation has put Baghdad in a difficult position: denouncing breaches of Iraqi sovereignty while also facing demands from its neighbors to prohibit armed groups from exploiting Iraqi territory to threaten them.

For Al-Zaidi, the September 30 withdrawal may fundamentally alter that equation.

Once the coalition mission is over, Iran-aligned elements will find it more difficult to justify maintaining autonomous military capabilities by citing the presence of foreign soldiers.

Baghdad will then have to decide whether it can impose its notion of a single armed authority in Iraq.

That problem is especially critical since Al-Zaidi is aiming to shift Iraq’s focus from decades of war and proxy conflict to rebuilding, investment, and closer economic ties with the US, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Jordan, and other foreign allies.

Repeated militia assaults risk undercutting that plan by raising investor anxiety and subjecting Iraq to reprisal for military choices that its government claims were not authorized.

The coalition’s exit therefore means more than just the removal of foreign troops.

It might serve as the catalyst for a far wider debate over who eventually controls Iraq’s armaments and war-making choices.

Baghdad will find it easy to declare complete sovereignty on October 1.

Demonstrating it will be far more difficult.

If Al-Zaidi is serious about guaranteeing that no foreign military presence stays in Iraq, the same sovereignty concept will increasingly be expected to apply to armed forces whose allegiance, weapons, or choices are not under the control of the Iraqi state.

Bringing such weapons under state control might prove to be one of the most important—and difficult—tests of Al-Zaidi’s leadership.

World.title: UAE’s ADNOC helps keep Iraqi oil flowing through Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is collaborating with the UAE’s ADNOC and other international energy merchants to maintain crude exports flowing through the Strait of Hormuz, as Baghdad seeks methods to secure key oil income amidst ongoing disruptions to Gulf shipping.

Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) reported that Abu Dhabi National Oil Company is one of the firms purchasing Iraqi petroleum and successfully transporting shipments over the strait.

According to Bloomberg, ADNOC’s trading arm is supplying Iraqi oil to Asian refiners via a shuttle system meant to mitigate the dangers involved with shipping bigger tankers into the Gulf.

Under the deal, smaller boats carry Iraqi Basrah oil via Hormuz before transferring the cargo to bigger tankers for delivery to Asian markets.

Tracking devices may also be turned off throughout sections of the route as ships negotiate the increasingly tough maritime environment.

The agreement is especially significant for Iraq, which relies heavily on oil exports to fund government expenditures.

The disruption at Hormuz has placed pressure on Baghdad to find methods to preserve exports while also ensuring the funds required to satisfy wages and other governmental commitments.

ADNOC’s cooperation gives Iraq another path to keep petroleum to overseas buyers while regular tanker operations are limited.

The move also follows the UAE’s exit from OPEC and OPEC+, which has given Abu Dhabi more control over its oil production and commercial strategy as it aims to boost output, trading activity, and energy income.

For Iraq, the immediate imperative is different but as important: keep crude flowing.

Baghdad is seeking longer-term options via Turkey and even the Mediterranean to minimize its reliance on Hormuz. However, until such routes are completely built, Iraq remains very vulnerable to Gulf disturbances.

The utilization of shuttle tankers and ship-to-ship transfers provides a temporary but potentially essential solution, allowing Iraq to keep access to Asian clients while also preserving the oil earnings that underpin much of the country’s economy.

World.title: Senior Iraqi security delegation heads to Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A high-level Iraqi security delegation will travel to Riyadh on Thursday, August 13, 2026, to conduct talks regarding recent cross-border drone strikes targeting petroleum infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, according to a senior government source.

The delegation will be led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari, Director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, alongside Iraqi National Intelligence Service (INIS) Chief Hamid Al-Shatri. The trip follows a reciprocal visit to Baghdad days earlier by Saudi Intelligence Chief Khalid bin Ali Al-Humaidan.

Key Security & Diplomatic Developments

High-Level Delegation: Led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari and Intelligence Chief Hamid Al-Shatri to establish joint intelligence-sharing protocols with Riyadh.

Incident Background: Late last month, the Saudi Ministry of Defense reported intercepting several drones originating from Iraqi territory targeting oil facilities in the Eastern Province and Riyadh.

Domestic Investigation: Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief Ali Falih al-Zaidi ordered a formal military investigation into the launch origins following the Saudi allegations.

Diplomatic Mediation: The visit comes after international and regional mediation restored diplomatic channels following the cancellation of Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s planned trip to Riyadh late last month amid joint U.S.-Saudi strikes inside Iraq.

Regional Position: During a recent bilateral meeting in Amman between Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan and Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein, Riyadh reaffirmed support for Iraq while stressing the necessity that Iraqi territory not be utilized as a platform for aggression against neighboring states.

The bilateral security summit aims to reinforce radar tracking, anti-drone intelligence sharing, and border surveillance between Baghdad and Riyadh.

While the “Islamic Resistance in Iraq” denied responsibility for the Saudi oil facility strikes, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s administration is taking direct steps to prevent unauthorized non-state launches, safeguard Iraqi sovereignty, and protect diplomatic and economic ties with Riyadh.

World.title: Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zidan to visit Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — President of the Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council, Judge Faiq Zidan, is scheduled to conduct an official visit to Syria on Thursday, August 13, 2026, marking a landmark first-of-its-kind judicial mission to Damascus, according to a senior official source.

The high-level visit aims to hold structured talks with Syrian judicial authorities to address shared legal frameworks, cross-border judicial coordination, counter-terrorism extradition agreements, and legal mechanisms regulating bilateral trade corridors.

World.title: Iraq Transport Ministry reports 95% completion of Development Road designs
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Minister of Transport Wahab Al-Hasani met with the Parliamentary Transport and Communications Committee on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, to review execution milestones across strategic infrastructure projects, including the Development Road, the Grand Fao Port, and national rail modernization.

During the executive session, Al-Hasani presented technical updates on the 1,200-kilometer Development Road Project, confirming that primary design phases are near completion, with railway engineering blueprints reaching 95% and highway transit designs at 85%.

Key Operational Metrics & Project Milestones

Development Road Project: Designs for the 1,200 km transit corridor are nearly complete (95% for railway tracks, 85% for highways). The MOU executed with Turkey serves as a preliminary framework with no current financial or legal obligations.

Grand Fao Port: Submerged tunnel construction reached 86% completion, alongside advanced structural work across five main container berths.

Rail Network Modernization: Ministry teams are actively pursuing the rehabilitation of the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia railway corridor extending toward the Syrian border.

Maritime Fleet Mobilization: State maritime companies confirmed readiness to deploy Iraqi vessels to transport crude oil and refined petroleum products to support alternative national export strategies.

Administrative & Executive Actions: Al-Hasani confirmed the suspension of Iraqi Airways’ former Director-General and two deputies following an internal investigative audit.

Legislative Alignment: Agreement reached to draft amendments to Transport Law No. 80 of 1983 and establish a joint parliamentary-executive committee holding weekly meetings to update transport regulations.

The meeting highlights Iraq’s strategy to transform into a central logistics bridge connecting the Gulf to Europe, bypassing maritime transit chokepoints.

By pairing the Grand Fao Port’s advancing infrastructure with overland rail links extending north to Turkey and west through the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia line toward Syria, the Ministry of Transport is laying the groundwork for integrated commercial supply chains across Eurasia.

World.title: MP Abdul Jabbar proposes 145 km pipeline to boost Basra crude to Ceyhan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Independent MP and Secretary-General of the Fao–Zakho Coalition, Amer Abdul-Jabbar, proposed a plan on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, to construct a 145-kilometer oil pipeline link to transport Basra crude north toward Turkey’s Ceyhan terminal.

Abdul-Jabbar stated via social media that the proposed missing link would instantly increase Iraq’s northern export capacity by 150,000 to 300,000 barrels per day (bpd). To avoid drawing on the federal budget during the ongoing liquidity crisis, he advocated launching a “National Volunteer Effort,” utilizing surplus piping from state-owned enterprises alongside logistical backing from private contractors operating under Ministry of Oil contracts.

Key Technical & Strategy Highlights

Proposed Pipeline Link: A 145 km strategic bypass connecting southern oilfields in Basra directly to northern export routes toward the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Capacity Increase: Designed to boost crude export flows by 150,000 to 300,000 bpd, mitigating bottlenecks caused by Persian Gulf shipping disruptions.

Zero-Cost Volunteer Framework: Proposed execution via a “National Volunteer Effort” using inventory audits of unused piping across state firms and private sector contractor support.

Existing Ministry Export Strategy: Complements Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair’s August 9 plan to export 750,000 bpd to Ceyhan via: 450,000 bpd pumped through the Strategic Pipeline after rehabilitating the PS3 pump station in Najaf and K3 in Haditha. 300,000 bpd transported via road tankers (including 200,000 bpd through KAR Group and 100,000 bpd under a secondary contract).

Long-Term Iraqi-Turkish Energy Framework: Ministry of Oil is finalizing a 1-year interim agreement with Ankara, paving the way for a 10- to 20-year strategic partnership involving Turkish BOTAŞ and BP in developing Kirkuk oilfields.

Abdul-Jabbar’s proposal comes as the Ministry of Oil accelerates alternative land-based export channels to bypass the blocked Strait of Hormuz.

Minister Khudair previously confirmed that Iraq’s State Company for Oil Projects (SCOP) and Turkey’s BOTAŞ are actively inspecting and rehabilitating the northern export system to handle between 500,000 and 750,000 bpd. Implementing the 145 km bypass link could offer Baghdad an immediate, low-cost mechanism to restore crude cash flows while long-term pipeline infrastructure is constructed toward Syria and Jordan.

World.title: Meta meets its own ‘tobacco’ moment in court
World.content:
Oakland – With billions of users around the world, Meta will defend itself against allegations of harming children in a new trial in the United States this week, which experts describe as social media’s big tobacco moment.

After a coalition of states sued Meta in 2023 for allegedly designing addictive features for kids in its apps, four states were selected to represent their claims: California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey.

Top prosecutors of those states now aim to prove in federal court that Meta deliberately made Facebook and Instagram addictive for children.

Meta “strongly disagrees with these allegations” and is “confident the evidence will show our longstanding commitment to supporting young people,” a spokesperson told AFP, adding that the company has “listened to parents, worked with experts and law enforcement.”

Although it’s not the first lawsuit that seeks to hold a social media company accountable for its impact on mental health and safety, it could become one of the most consequential.

“It really feels like tobacco in the 1990s,” Vincent Joralemon, a director at Berkeley’s Life Sciences Law and Policy Center, told AFP.

While these cases about social media harms revolve around the intersection of technology and addiction, the legal argument in this case against Meta centers on its business practices, just like when the federal government sued tobacco companies around three decades ago, Joralemon said.

By the early 1990s, decades of research showed that tobacco use caused health problems such as cancer, and eventually additional investigations revealed how the industry deliberately downplayed, and even concealed, the harmful impacts of its products.

– ‘Protecting teens’ –

Dozens of US states sued four major tobacco companies, and by 1998, won a landmark settlement agreement which included financial penalties and changes to how products were marketed, particularly to children whom the industry targeted with s featuring cartoon characters, the most famous of which was known as “Joe Camel.”

Jury selection begins today in Oakland, a short drive from San Francisco and opening statements are expected to begin August 18.

Meta was convicted on similar grounds in separate trials held in Los Angeles and New Mexico, with combined damages that approach $1 billion.

In Oakland, the states are demanding a long list of changes to Meta’s apps, in addition to financial penalties as high as $1.4 trillion, close to Meta’s entire market value which hovers around $1.5 trillion.

Despite the eye-popping number, money isn’t Meta’s biggest problem, if it were to lose the case.

“The huge issue here is reputational harm” and being forced to make major changes, Joralemon said.

“Putting a CEO on the witness stand can be quite damning,” as well, he said.

Meta founder and chief Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses expected to testify.

The case could be “the beginning of a broader reckoning” for Meta, Nora Freeman Engstrom told AFP via email. She is a law professor and associate dean at Stanford.

It will be important to see the “gap” between what Meta knew privately and what it disclosed publicly, Engstrom said.

Meta is “confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts,” Meta told AFP last week.

With so many plaintiffs suing Meta and other social media companies, these lawsuits could potentially “go on for decades,” Joralemon said.

In May, Snap, TikTok, YouTube and Meta settled with a school district in Kentucky for $27 million to avoid another trial that was expected to set a precedent for around 1,200 similar lawsuits.

On Monday, a federal appeals court ruled that more than 3,000 additional lawsuits filed against Meta, YouTube-parent Google, Snap and TikTok can proceed.

World.title: Colombia rescuers find woman alive as quake death toll passes 240
World.content:
Pereira – Colombian rescuers pulled a 32-year-old woman alive from the rubble of a collapsed building Tuesday, sparking cheers and applause as exhausted crews raced to find more survivors from the country’s strongest earthquake in a century.

Daniela Largo was carried from the wreckage wrapped in a blue blanket as rescuers embraced and relatives shouted out with joy.

The rescue came as soldiers, firefighters and volunteers searched collapsed buildings across western Colombia after a 7.4-magnitude quake killed at least 241 people and injured more than 1,600.

“We were losing hope and then we received a call,” said her mother Sandra Milena Perez in Pereira.

Perez said a local resident heard cries for help beneath the rubble and joined neighbors in removing debris before professional rescuers arrived.

“Thanks to him, today we’re happy,” she said. “At home her 12-year-old son is waiting for her.”

In Pereira and in Cali, emergency crews used cranes, dogs and heavy machinery to search ruined buildings while volunteers formed human chains to clear debris by hand, hoping to reach people still trapped beneath collapsed structures.

As darkness fell, families prepared to sleep in parks as aftershocks rattled damaged neighborhoods where entire blocks had been reduced to rubble.

The quake overwhelmed parts of the health system, turning the rescue effort into one of Colombia’s largest disaster responses in years.

“The house came down on top of us. I wasn’t able to get out,” said Beatriz Arcos, who was trapped with her husband and mother beneath their collapsed condominium.

“It took about an hour to get us out.” Arcos said she was hospitalized after a concrete block fell on her back. Her husband and mother were also injured.

In Cali, residents armed with picks, shovels and their bare hands joined firefighters in digging through collapsed buildings.

Rescuers stopped every few minutes to call into the rubble and listen for any response.

“We’re doing this with our hands, with gloves” said volunteer Pablo Cesar Ruiz “It’s sad to see time slipping away.”

In Pereira, army units and sniffer dogs combed through twisted concrete and exposed steel.

At one site, a rescue squad leader abruptly raised his fist, stopping workers so they could listen for signs of life.

Volunteers formed human chains, passing bricks and chunks of masonry hand-to-hand to clear paths into collapsed structures.

– ‘So much effort’ –

For many families, the desperate search was becoming a vigil.

“My aunt lived there. She’s under the rubble,” said Jorge Gonzalez, standing beside a collapsed building in Pereira.

“I arrived yesterday and I haven’t left, and until they find her body I don’t intend to leave here.”

While some families waited for news of missing relatives, others were grappling with the loss of homes, possessions and livelihoods.

“We lost everything,” said Stella Galvis, fighting back tears after escaping the collapse of her home.

“We survived by a miracle, since I managed to get my little boy out and my partner managed to get out too.”

From the air, neighborhoods in Cali appeared flattened, with piles of grey rubble replacing entire blocks of homes and apartment buildings.

Nearby, cars lay crushed beneath fallen walls and concrete slabs.

On one mound of debris, a young couple climbed over broken masonry searching for belongings.

They recovered a box from inside a child’s bright red bedside table.

Many survivors spent the night outdoors, either because their homes were damaged or because they feared aftershocks.

One park in Pereira was transformed into a makeshift shelter with tents and mattresses.

“We lost everything, but we’re alive,” said 23-year-old John Tabasco, who was camped there with his wife and seven-month-old son.

“We’ve never had to do this before, to depend on someone else to help us. It’s amazing how life can change.”

Others struggled to come to terms with losing homes built over decades.

“You buy a little house with so much effort, spending 40, 50 years struggling to get yourself that house, you finally get it and in just a few days it all goes down the drain,” said 79-year-old Jaime Alzate.

In Cali, part of the Hospital Universitario del Valle collapsed during the quake, forcing doctors to move patients into a parking lot and treat some in the open air.

Yet amid the destruction, many Colombians mobilized to help.

Thousands brought water, food and supplies to affected neighborhoods, while long lines formed outside blood donation centers.

“It’s about wanting to help your community, your city and your country,” said blood donor Ferney Cabrera.

President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency and promised rent subsidies for affected families Tuesday during a visit to Pereira.

The United States announced $15.5 million in emergency aid, while messages of support and offers of assistance arrived from around the world.

As aftershocks continued to rattle damaged cities, rescue crews pressed on through the ruins, hoping more voices, taps or whistles might still emerge.

World.title: 'No NALSAR 2026 graduate will be enrolled as advocate': BCI amid CJI convocation invite row
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Bar Council of India (BCI) has directed all state bar councils to halt the enrolment of any 2026 law graduate from NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad, as an advocate until further orders.

This follows an alleged organised campaign against the participation of Chief Justice Surya Kant in the universityâs convocation ceremony.

The directive was issued by bar council chairman Manan Kumar Mishra, who said the Council had taken note of reports and material in the public domain regarding an organised campaign at NALSAR's convocation ceremony.

The bar council has also sought an authenticated factual report from the university within three days and said the matter will be considered on August 19, after the vice-chancellor submits the report.

The council has asked NALSAR to identify, on the basis of verifiable material, the persons allegedly instrumental in initiating, drafting, circulating, coordinating or mobilising the campaign. It has sought details of those involved in organising meetings, communicating with the media, administering social media or organised groups used for coordination, or proposing or mobilising any call for boycott, obstruction, disruption or organised non-participation in the convocation or any programme connected with the CJI.





The bar council has also sought information on whether any student body, student bar council, studentsâ union or other recognised student organisation was involved in initiating, approving, coordinating or circulating the campaign. The university has also been asked to specify whether any faculty member, research scholar, alumnus or outsider participated in initiating, drafting, coordinating, advising or facilitating the campaign.

It said a distinction must be maintained between those who merely signed or supported a representation and those who organised or coordinated the campaign or proposed or mobilised an actual boycott, obstruction or disruption.

World.title: From erotic fantasy to Indian identity, a famous Italian calendar finds a new story
World.content:
Behind-the-scenes image featuring Avani Rai (left) during the Pirelli Calendar shoot in Delhi I Picture credit: Alessandro Scotti

One half of the 2027 Pirelli Calendar features Indian celebrities photographed by Norwegian photographer SÃ¸lve SundsbÃ¸ I Picture credit: Alessandro Scotti

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

In 1966, a photograph of a woman in underwear arrived at the Vatican. The fashion imagery might seem rather tame by today's standards, but it was enough to provoke an official complaint from the Holy See to an Italian tire company called Pirelli. The Milan-based tire manufacturer had just begun producing these exclusive, high-fashion calendars, simply called 'The Cal', as a trade gift for its top clients â the idea being to give VIPs something a cut above the cheap pin-up calendars that were standard fare in garages and tire shops at the time.But the condemnation had the opposite effect. Rather than suppressing the calendar, it generated enormous publicity, transforming a niche corporate giveaway into one of the world's most coveted cultural status symbols. Within a few years, the calendar became less a marketing gimmick and more an annual referendum on where European ideas of beauty, sex and provocation stood. Over the decades, figures from Naomi Campbell, Cindy Crawford and Kate Moss to PenÃ©lope Cruz, Serena Williams and Yoko Ono have been framed within its pages by some of the world's most influential photographers. But sixty-two years and a great many controversies later, the most recent edition of that same calendar is shot not on a Mediterranean beach or a Manhattan studio, but in the forts and villages of Rajasthan and the mean streets of Old Delhi, even featuring everyday barbers and artisans.The 2027 Pirelli Calendar is dedicated to India. For the first time, it features an all-India cast and is shot entirely in the country, built around the idea of Indian identity. So alongside glamorous portraits of celebrities like television host and author Padma Lakshmi, actress Aditi Rao Hydari, sitarist Anoushka Shankar and supermodel Bhavitha Mandava are some 200 ordinary Indians, from dancers and street artists to musicians and craftspeople.The project began as a collaboration between Norwegian photographer SÃ¸lve SundsbÃ¸ and Raghu Rai, modern India's most celebrated photojournalist known for chronicling the country's many faces and contradictions over several decades. Rai died in April shortly after the project began. His daughter, photographer Avani Rai, stepped in to complete it and in doing so changed its direction. What had been conceived as a studio shoot moved outdoors into the neighbourhoods her father spent his career documenting, from Kinari Bazar and Yamuna Ghat to the streets of Old Delhi.When asked how a project like the Pirelli Calendar sits alongside her reportage-driven practice, Avani, speaking to TOI, gently rejects the premise of the question. Genre, she argues, describes where a photograph ends up, not how it is made. What remains constant, whether in documentary work or a fashion commission, is the attempt to stay honest to what is in front of the camera. "Curiosity, presence and empathy are not specific to one genre of photography. The Pirelli Calendar asked me to bring those values into a different context. I wasnât interested in making images that simply looked beautiful. I wanted them to feel alive. To hold the same emotional honesty that I search for in every photograph I make," says Avani whose mother, conservation architect Gurmeet Rai, also appears in the calendar.Even to this day, The Cal's physical copies are not sold publicly; Pirelli limits production to roughly 20,000 copies annually and they are sent as corporate gifts to monarchs, CEOs, prime ministers, top celebrities, fashion icons and the like.But why India? SundsbÃ¸ says it was a long-held ambition within Pirelli. His contribution came from a very different vantage pointâthat of an outsider conscious of his own limitations. "The fact that Avani and Raghu Raiâs images would be one half of the Calendar enabled me to concentrate on portraits. That's a smaller and more realistic task for a visitor than capturing the whole soul of a nation.I didnât try to decide what âIndiannessâ should mean. Especially not as the guest that I am. I tried to cast people I admire, women who have inspirational talent," says SundsbÃ¸.The edition also marks the first time Pirelli has commissioned two photographers to share a calendar. What makes the India edition notable is not simply that it swaps eroticism for cultural identity; the calendar has been moving in that direction for years. Rather, it is the first edition shaped by two intertwined perspectives: an outsider looking in and a daughter completing her father's final project in the streets he loved."I used to think inheritance was about continuing someoneâs work. Now I think itâs about continuing their way of being in the world. The patience they lived with. The integrity they carried. The generosity with which they met people. Those are the things that survive," says Avani."Completing the calendar gave me a sense of continuity. It wasnât about recreating him or holding onto the past. I understood that what he had really left me wasnât an archive or even a body of work. It was a practice of being alive to the world," she adds.

World.title: 'Modi thinks foreign policy is this': Rahul mocks PM; another Congress leader takes Meloni swipe
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Thursday took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs foreign policy, suggesting that the PMâs diplomacy is overly associated with hugging foreign leaders.

Speaking at the Rachnatmak Congress national convention, Rahul said, âI donât know where he got this idea from. Strange ideas get into peopleâs heads. He thinks this is foreign policy,â before giving a big hug to Congress leader Sandeep Dikshit.

Dikshit then quipped, âYou werenât hugging me thinking I was Meloni?â Rahul replied, âI havenât reached that stage yet,â drawing laughter from the gathering.

Rahul then returned to his criticism, saying, âI donât know where he got this idea that foreign policy means hugging leaders.â

He also questioned India-US relations, pointing to Pakistanâs role in mediating during the Iran war and raising questions over Indiaâs diplomatic positioning amid the ongoing West Asia conflict.

"War broke out in Iran. For Indiaâhad it recognized its own strength and had its leader been someone like Indira Gandhiâthis presented the greatest opportunity in the world. What kind of opportunity? Iran was our old friend, America was our friend, and Russia was our friend.





We could have stepped up, become relevant, and leveraged these friendships. But what actually happened? Nothing of the sort. Instead, Pakistan stepped in and took our place; Pakistan became the mediator, while India and Modi-ji simply looked on," he said.

Speaking about China, Rahul said, "I receive information directly from Modi jiâs office these days; there is a full-blown revolt going on inside. In our patrolling areasâspecifically in ArunachalâChina blocked us from patrolling.

They essentially said, 'Look, all that is fineâit is indeed your landâbut you cannot patrol here'".

BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj slammed Rahul and called the remarks "uncultured, undignified, obscene and indecent".

"The uncultured, undignified, obscene and indecent remarks Rahul Gandhi made about Prime Minister Narendra Modi today made him look less like the leader of the opposition and more like a failed stand-up comedian. He was resorting to locker-room talk and cheap innuendos. The leader of the opposition has a very important role in any democracy. India deserves a better Leader of the Opposition than a 54-year-old man behaving in a juvenile manner," she said.

Rahul Gandhi has repeatedly criticised the PM Modi governmentâs handling of the West Asia crisis, particularly its response to US President Donald Trumpâs statements and actions in the region.

World.title: Bengal govt strips BJP MP Ananta Maharaj of Banga Bibhushan award over 'insulting' remarks against Netaji
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The West Bengal government on Thursday withdrew the Banga Bibhushan award from BJP Rajya Sabha member Ananta Maharaj over his alleged derogatory comment against Netaji.

Banga Bibhushan is one of West Bengalâs highest civilian honours, awarded by the state government to eminent personalities for outstanding contributions in fields such as art, culture, literature, social service and other areas. Ananta Maharaj was conferred the Banga Bibhushan on February 21 this year, by then-West Bengal chief minister

at a state government programme in Kolkata marking International Mother Language Day; which has now been revoked.

The controversy erupted after BJP Rajya Sabha MP Nagendra Roy, alias Ananta Maharaj, questioned Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's role in forming and leading the Azad Hind Fauj. Speaking at a meeting in Dinhata on July 19, Roy asked, âDid Netaji have the capacity to organise and form the Azad Hind Fauj?â He then claimed that âthey were all British soldiersâ and alleged that âthe Indian National Army (INA) was misused.â

Roy also claimed that the Azad Hind Fauj originated from British-Indian troops who had been handed over by Germany.





His remarks triggered a backlash in West Bengal, with political leaders and Rajbanshi organisations condemning the comments and demanding action against the BJP MP. Prominent Rajbanshi figures issued a joint statement condemning the remarks as false, insulting and damaging to social harmony. Forward Bloc, a party founded by Netaji, also lodged police complaints and demanded the immediate revocation of his Rajya Sabha membership.

World.title: 'This is your last chance': SC ultimatum to Centre over delay in front-of-pack food warning labels
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday sharply criticised the Centre and the

(

) over the delay in introducing front-of-pack warning labels for packaged food products high in sugar, salt and saturated fat, warning that it would issue directions if the government failed to take a final decision.

A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran gave the Centre two weeks to place its final decision on record, making it clear that the government could either implement the proposed warning labels on its own or face judicial intervention.

"This is your last chance. Next time we will dictate the judgment," the bench said, according to ANI.

The court repeatedly underlined that the issue was one of public health, particularly the health of children and questioned the government's reluctance to move ahead with stronger nutritional warnings.

"Why? You don't want people of this country to remain healthy? More particularly growing children?" the bench asked during the hearing.

Appearing for the Centre, additional solicitor general Brijender Chahar argued that applying strict warning standards could create complications for traditional Indian food items. He said products such as namkeen could end up carrying red warning symbols because of their fat or salt content.





He also argued that international nutritional standards might not be directly applicable to Indian dietary habits, pointing out that even two eggs could exceed the prescribed daily fat limit.

The court, however, was unconvinced.

The bench said consumers were already aware that packaged foods contained sugar, fat and carbohydrates, but front-of-pack warning labels would provide a simpler and more effective way of communicating nutritional risks before a purchase was made.

The judges also rejected the argument that warning labels could adversely affect manufacturers.

According to ANI, the bench observed that the final decision to purchase a product would continue to rest with consumers and that commercial considerations could not take precedence over public health.

During the proceedings, senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for a manufacturer, attempted to make submissions.

The court responded by stating that the case concerned the health of citizens and that manufacturers could not determine government policy on the issue.

Senior advocate Devadutt Kamat suggested that food products could be categorised differently and that detailed nutritional information should be displayed.

The bench clarified that it was not opposed to any particular food product but was only seeking greater consumer awareness.

"In this country, how many people can afford dry fruits? And how many children buy Kurkure? That makes all the difference. We are not against any particular product. We only want the person purchasing it to know what he is consuming," the court said, according to ANI.

The bench also referred to its February 10, 2026, order, in which it had previously addressed the issue and laid down its observations.

During Thursday's hearing, the petitioner's counsel drew the court's attention to the minutes of an FSSAI meeting held on March 7, which allegedly reflected a position contrary to the suggestions made by the court earlier.

The judges also took exception to the Centre's argument that India could not easily adopt international standards relating to nutritional warnings.

"We do not approve the stance of the Union when it says that it's not possible to match the international standards, more particularly developed countries. Should India remain an undeveloped country?" the bench asked, according to ANI.

"The world should know that India is concerned about the health of its citizens and more particularly children," it added.

The case stems from a petition seeking mandatory front-of-pack warning labels for packaged food products containing high levels of sugar, salt and saturated fat.

The proposed labels are intended to help consumers quickly identify potentially unhealthy products before buying them.

The issue has also been discussed by Parliament's Committee on Subordinate Legislation, headed by Shiv Sena Rajya Sabha MP Milind Deora, who has advocated studying Singapore's Nutri-Grade model as a possible template for India.

Separately, the Union health ministry has proposed displaying "sugar and oil boards" in schools, offices and other public institutions as part of a broader effort to encourage healthier eating habits and reduce excessive consumption of sugar and oil.

World.title: Watch: When gunman tried to assassinate Sukhbir Badal at Golden Temple in 2024
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Sukhbir Singh Badalâs Thursday attack in Nanded marks the second serious attempt on the Shiromani Akali Dal leaderâs life. The SAD leader was also attacked two years ago at the Golden Temple when a gunman opened fire at him while Badal was serving religious punishment at the shrine.

On December 4, 2024, Badal was attacked at the entrance of the temple, where he was seated in a wheelchair because of his fractured leg, during a penance ordered by the Akal Takht. Video footage from the incident shows the moment the attacker overpowered him within seconds.

The footage showed him dressed in a blue sewadar uniform. He was stationed at the temple entrance as part of the punishment pronounced by the Akal Takht over alleged misconduct during his tenure from 2007 to 2017.

As Badal sat with a placard around his neck, a man who was later identified as Narayan Singh Chaura approached him and opened fire. The attempt, however, was foiled almost immediately.

In the clip, right after the gunman pulled out the weapon, an alert sewadar, believed to be a volunteer associated with an Akali leader, intervened and pushed the assailantâs arm upward as he attempted to fire. The bullet was discharged harmlessly into the air, and the attacker was quickly overpowered by volunteers and others present at the scene.





Police personnel stationed at the shrine also moved in and apprehended Chaura on the spot. Confirming the swift response, ADCP Harpal Singh said, âNo one was injured in the attack.â

It was not long after the attempted attack that other sewadars present at the scene assembled together to create a human shield around Badal.

Despite the dramatic shooting attempt, Badal remained calm.

Still seated in his wheelchair, he continued performing his duties as a sewadar, holding a spear and staying at the temple entrance after the assailant had been detained.

In a separate clip, the shooter could be seen being overpowered by the crowd. The people holding the man can be heard asking him his motive for opening fire on the SAD leader.

The religious punishment had been announced on December 2, 2024, by Sikh high priests for Badal and other Akali leaders in connection with incidents of sacrilege and the pardon granted to controversial Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim. The tankhah was part of a reconciliation process led by Sikh religious authorities to address long-standing grievances within the community.

With Wednesdayâs attack once again putting security arrangements at the Golden Temple under scrutiny, the earlier firing incident has returned to focus as a reminder that this was not the first time Sukhbir Singh Badal was targeted while performing religious service at Sikhismâs holiest shrine.

World.content:

NEW DELHI: Air India group has from Thursday started 'mandatory substance screening' for all pilots following the Phuket-Delhi flight serious incident. The move comes to âprotect and sustainâ the trust AI had earned over the decades that has been shaken by the pilot-in-command of the Phuket flight testing positive for marijuana. Aviation secretary Samir Sinha had in clear terms asked AI to âtake responsibilityâ and do whatever it takes to ensure safety.AI senior VP (flight operations) captain Manish Uppal wrote to all pilots on Thursday: âFor decades, Air India has been the flag bearer of Indian aviation. Over this time the professionalism, skill and commitment to safety of our pilots, together with other staff, has earned the trust of millions of passengers and the wider community. This trust is our most important asset, and it is vital that we do all possible to protect and sustain it. Many of you have recently reached out to share the same sentiment.ââAs you know, Air India already fully complies with all regulatory requirements prescribed by India's DGCA, which are similar to those practiced in other major aviation jurisdictions including Europe and the US. We nevertheless now feel it is important to go further.Accordingly we have decided to undertake a full screening of all group pilots for any substances or medications that are not permitted under prevailing regulations. This testing is mandatory and will start today, 13 August 2026.ââIt will be conducted concurrently with training at the Gurugram Academy, post flight at our Flight Briefing Centres / Air India Offices, or at locations provided by your respective bases. This initiative, which goes beyond regulatory requirements, reflects our determination to uphold the highest standards of safety and professionalism, and to provide reassurance to our passengers, stakeholders and the community at large. Thank you for your continued professionalism, dedication and commitment to maintaining the trust placed in Air India. Should you require any clarification, contact your Chief Pilot and/or Base Manager,â it says.

World.title: Truckers call 24-hour strike on NH-37 to Manipur
World.content:
Truckers stopped operations on National Highway-37 in Manipur on Thursday (August 13, 2026) following the death of a stranded driver on the highway, even as the State government pushed for the reopening of other highways in the State.

NH-37, the least blockade-prone highway in Manipur, connects State capital Imphal with Silchar in southern Assam. Truckers have been stranded on this highway for almost a month due to sporadic blockades and landslides in Manipur.

A loose associationof truck operators called a 24-hour strike on the movement of goods on NH-37 on Thursday (August 13, 2026) after Nagina Kumar Mahto, a driver from Narayanpur in Bihar, died near Labankhal in Jiribam district in the State.

The truckers said Mahto did not respond to calls on his mobile phone and was later found unconscious in his vehicle on Wednesday. He was rushed to the Jiribam Primary Health Centre, where the doctor on duty declared him dead.

“We want the governments of India, Assam, and Manipur to address our concerns and compensate the deceased driver’s family adequately,” one of the striking drivers said.

Manipur government announces reopening of National Highways

The drivers also accused the authorities of ignoring their prolonged ordeal. “We have to be on the roads for weeks without proper food, drinking water, or medical assistance. We are paying a heavy price and risking our lives to transport essential commodities to a State in conflict,” a trucker in Jiribam said. Jiribam is close to the Assam-Manipur border.

The truckers warned that their strike could be extended if the government failed to address issues they faced. Officials in Jiribam said the cause of Mahto’s death could be ascertained after an autopsy.

On August 8, Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh announced the reopening of the State’s arterial highways for all communities. While tribal organisations responded by lifting their blockade on NH-202 (connecting Imphal and Naga-dominated Ukhrul district), there has been no such move on NH-2, which links Imphal and Nagaland’s capital Kohima.

Movement on NH-2, the most preferred lifeline of Manipur, remains restricted for members of certain communities since the ethnic conflict between the Kuki-Zo and Meitei people broke out in May 2023.

World.title: BMRCL to temporarily close Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Metro Station on Independence Day
World.content:
The Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) has announced the temporary closure of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Metro Station (Vidhana Soudha) on Saturday (August 15), in view of the Independence Day ‘Freedom Habba’ celebrations at Vidhana Soudha.

According to a media release issued by BMRCL, the station will remain closed for both entry and exit from 10 a.m. to 9.30 p.m. as part of crowd management and public safety measures. Metro trains, however, will continue to operate on the route and pass through the station without stopping.

BMRCL said that the entry into the station will be permitted from 9.30 p.m. to facilitate the movement of passengers after the event. However, exit from the station will continue to remain restricted until 10 p.m.

To handle the expected increase in passenger traffic after the celebrations, BMRCL said that additional Metro services would be operated, if required.

Passengers travelling during the closure period have been advised to use Cubbon Park Metro Station or Sir M. Visvesvaraya Metro Station, Central College, as alternative stations.

The temporary arrangements have been made following directions from the Commissioner, Bengaluru Central City Corporation.

World.title: ‘Sravana Masam’ celebrations begin on grand note at Srisailam
World.content:
The auspicious ‘Sravana Masam’ celebrations began on a grand note at the Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy temple in Srisailam on Thursday.

Srisailam temple Trust Board chairman Pothugunta Ramesh Naidu and executive officer M. Srinivasa Rao said that Sravana Masam celebrations will be held till September 12, and a large number of devotees are expected to visit the temple during this period. They said arrangements are being made for the accommodation, drinking water supply, comfortable ‘darshan’ facilities, ‘Arjitha Sevas’ for the presiding deities on regular days, distribution of ‘Anna Prasadam’, sanitation, and vehicle parking.

For the convenience of ordinary devotees, ‘Garbhalaya Abhishekam’ (sanctum sanctorum anointing), ‘Samuhika Abhishekam’ (mass anointing), and ‘Kumkumarchana’ have been completely suspended on specific days during Sravana Masam, including Sravana Saturdays, Sundays, and Mondays, as well as ‘Varalakshmi Vratam’ and ‘Sravana Purnima’ (totalling 19 days).

‘Udayastamana Seva’, ‘Pratahkala Seva’, and ‘Pradosha Kala Seva’ have been fully suspended. On these days, ‘Sparsha Darshan’ of the deity would be permitted only during the night hours. Additionally, Garbhalaya Abhishekam during the morning hours has been suspended on August 18, September 1, and September 8 (all Tuesdays). On other ordinary days during the month of Sravana, Arjita Abhishekam, Samuhika Abhishekam, and Kumkumarchana will continue as usual.

The Chairman and EO announced that free mass Varalakshmi Vratams (ritual prayers dedicated to Goddess Varalakshmi) would be conducted on three occasions during the holy month for the convenience of devotees. These mass Varalakshmi Vratams are scheduled for the second Friday (August 21), third Friday (August 28), and fourth Friday (September 4) of the Sravana month.

Each session of free Varalakshmi Vratam will accommodate 1,500 participants. The second session is specifically designated for 1,000 Shiva Sevaks (temple volunteers). The third session will specifically accommodate 750 married women from the Chenchu ​​community and 750 other married women.

World.title: ED attack case: Kerala High Court upholds bail for ninth accused
World.content:
The Kerala High Court has refused to interfere with the bail granted to Harish Kumar, one of the accused in the attack on Enforcement Directorate officials during a raid at Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan’s house in Thiruvananthapuram.

The Sessions Court, Thiruvananthapuram, had granted bail to Mr. Kumar in June. Recently, the court allowed the bail applications of 17 other accused as well, imposing conditions such as execution of a bond of ₹1 Lakh each, with two solvent sureties for an equivalent sum, and depositing ₹10,000 each before the Magistrate Court with jurisdiction.

Justice C.S. Dias noted that the condition to deposit ₹10,000 had not been imposed by the Sessions Court in Mr. Kumar’s bail, and modified his bail conditions to include the same.

Charges under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act, 1984 for assault and damage to official vehicles were laid against around 300 individuals in the alleged attack, of which 25 have been apprehended.

World.title: Alleged abduction of youth: Mattannur native arrested
World.content:
The Chevayur police have arrested a man in connection with the alleged abduction and extortion of a 21-year-old person, who was reportedly held captive and threatened with circulation of private videos unless his family paid ₹8 lakh.

The arrested is Jishnu Jayan, a native of Mattannur in Kannur. He was taken into custody from Kannur by a special squad on Wednesday (August 12, 2026).

The complainant, who had travelled to Bengaluru to meet a friend, alleged that a six-member gang had abducted him and recorded the videos before demanding the ransom.

According to the complaint received by the police, the youth travelled to Bengaluru on July 24, 2026, and was staying at his friend’s flat. He was allegedly taken out by the gang on the pretext of meeting another acquaintance.

They allegedly took him to an isolated location and confined him there. The accused allegedly recorded private videos of the youth and later sent the footage to his family members.

According to police sources, the abductors reportedly demanded ₹8 lakh from the family for his release and threatened to circulate more videos if the money was not paid. When the family refused to pay the ransom, the youth was allegedly assaulted.

The youth, in his petition, claimed that he managed to escape from the gang’s custody and returned to Kerala to move the legal way. He subsequently approached the Chevayur police and lodged a complaint.

Police sources said a woman and four other persons, in addition to the arrested person, were allegedly involved in the incident. They were found absconding following the intensified probe.

World.title: Flood revives Malarikkal’s pink bloom
World.content:
The floods may have left the backwater villages of Kottayam battered and bruised, but they have left Malarikkal blooming once again. As the waters recede, vast polders in the village are turning into a pink carpet of water lilies, drawing visitors in the early hours of the day.

The water lily season at Malarikkal, a popular monsoon attraction, had a rather subdued start this year following a weak monsoon. But the floods appear to have changed that, with the plants now bursting into full bloom.

“The floods, which are an annual phenomenon here, have been a blessing in disguise this time,” said K. Anil Kumar, convenor of the Meenachil-Meenanthara-Kodoor river relinking programme, which organises the annual Ambal Vasantham water lily festival at Malarikkal. The collective is also planning a host of new initiatives to further promote the destination, he said.

Floods clear weeds

The rising waters forced most villagers into relief camps for nearly a week in the first week of August and they have only recently begun returning home. “But the floods also washed away the weeds that had spread among the water lilies during the weak monsoon. The weeds had threatened to overwhelm the lily plants this season,” he said.

With the rains receding and the floodwaters draining away, visitors have begun trickling in to witness the spectacular bloom. The crowds are particularly heavy on holidays, with visitors arriving as early as 5.30 a.m. By 6 a.m., boats carrying tourists begin heading into the lily-filled polders, where the flowers remain in full bloom until around 9 a.m.

Around 80 country boats have been deployed to take visitors into the polders. With crowds already swelling, organisers have introduced restrictions to protect the blooms, particularly as some visitors have been plucking the flowers. Visitors have been asked to buy flower bundles from local residents and park their vehicles only in designated areas.

Boost for local economy

The steady influx of visitors is also giving the local economy a boost, providing income for villagers and boat operators, who can earn up to ₹30,000 a month during the season. Homestays in the area, too, have seen a rise in demand.

The water lily season is expected to last until late September or early October, after which the next cycle of paddy cultivation will begin. Water is usually drained from the J Block Ompathinayiram padashekaram, with preparations for cultivation beginning on the fifth day of the Malayalam month of Kanni.

Meanwhile, local farmers have already begun preparing for the next paddy season, constructing bunds to facilitate the draining of water from the fields.

World.title: Orthodox Church  to consult legal experts on Kerala HC order
World.content:
The Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church has welcomed the State government’s efforts to mediate in the long-running church dispute, saying it will cooperate with talks based on the Supreme Court judgment of July 3, 2017.

In a statement, Yuhanon Mar Dioscoros Metropolitan, president of the Orthodox Church Media Wing, said the church would consult legal experts before deciding on further steps regarding the recent High Court Division Bench judgment concerning five parish churches and a chapel in Palakkad, Ernakulam and Kollam districts.

The judgment concerns police protection for Cherukunnam St Thomas Orthodox Church, Mangalamp Dam St Mary’s Orthodox Church, and Erikkumchira St Mary’s Orthodox Church in Palakkad; Odakkali St Mary’s Orthodox Church and Attinkunnu Kurishupalli (chapel) in Ernakulam; and Mukathala St Stephen’s Orthodox Church in Kollam.

According to the metropolitan, the apex court had already made it clear that the 1934 Church constitution governs the churches of the Malankara Church. In the case of the places of worship covered by the latest judgment, the High Court has directed that the order be implemented through the civil court.

“The position of the Orthodox Church is that the law should be implemented through the courts. At the same time, we have always welcomed mediation efforts by the government to resolve the dispute amicably,” the Metropolitan said.

World.title: Kozhikode’s IMHANS, a leading mental healthcare institute, remains without full-time director
World.content:
The Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (IMHANS) in Kozhikode, a premier mental healthcare centre under the Health department in Kerala, is yet to get a full-time director after the demise of the incumbent P. Krishnakumar in 2025.

The IMHANS is an autonomous institution that has been functioning in areas of mental healthcare delivery, training, research, and policy development. According to sources, though the previous Left Democratic Front government had initiated a process to fill the vacancy, it could not be completed due to various reasons. Applications were invited from qualified persons under the Directorate of Medical Education and the Directorate of Health Services for the post. Even after a change of guard occurred in the State government, the recruitment is in limbo, it is learnt.

Higher officials in the department were not available for comments.

Dr. Krishnakumar, a long-time director of the institute, passed away in January 2025. For around five months, K.G. Sajeeth Kumar, Principal, Government Medical College, Kozhikode, was given the charge. V.P. Jithu, Head of the Department of Psychiatry, has been holding the responsibility thereafter.

Sources said on Thursday that the staff association at the IMHANS has suggested that T.M. Shibu Kumar, Associate Professor, Department of Psychiatry, Government Medical College Hospital, Kozhikode, be appointed to the post. They pointed out that this could benefit the institution as Dr. Shibu Kumar was familiar with its functioning.

The sources said a full-time director was essential to formulate new schemes in the mental healthcare sector and spearhead research initiatives. Patients from nearly all districts in north Kerala rely on the institute for their mental healthcare needs. The IMHANS provides outpatient services and runs an autism clinic, besides implementing community mental health programmes, child development services, and rehabilitation projects.

Other than this, the institute offers MPhil programmes in Psychiatric Social Work, Clinical Psychology and post-basic diploma in psychiatric nursing. MPhil (Psychiatric Social Work) was launched in 2014 and M.Phil (Clinical Psychology) in 2017, and a post-basic diploma course in psychiatric nursing is being run since 2014. All these courses were launched for the first time in the government sector in Kerala.

The institute got its own building when Dr. Krishnakumar was at its helm. Recognising the community projects taken up by it, the IMHANS was selected by the Union government to be elevated as a centre of excellence in mental health in its 11th plan.

World.title: Pakistan, Norway reaffirm resolve to strengthen bilateral ties, expand engagement in defence and security
World.content:
Pakistan and Norway on Thursday reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral ties and expanding cooperation in defence and security.

Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide, who is on a two-day visit to Pakistan, called on Chief of Defence Forces and the Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, with the two leaders reiterating their resolve to further strengthen bilateral ties and expand engagement in defence and security, according to a statement issued by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).

The two sides discussed matters of “mutual interest, regional security, and bilateral relations”.

During the meeting, Field Marshal Munir highlighted “Pakistan’s perspective on global peace and regional stability” and stressed the “importance of cooperation and collaborative efforts to address common security challenges”.

The Norwegian foreign minister appreciated the “professional role” played by the Pakistan Armed Forces “in promoting regional peace and stability”.

Earlier in the day, Eide addressed a press conference alongside Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar in Islamabad, during which he lauded Pakistan’s mediatory role in the US-Iran conflict, saying it was a “service to the world and hence, also to us”.

“I also really want to reiterate our strong support for the very important role that Pakistan has taken in this dramatic war that started on February 28 with the US-Israel attack on Iran,” he said, recalling that Norway was one of the Western countries that was “clearest and earliest” in stating that the war was a violation of international rules.

“If we stand up for international law, it has to apply to everyone, everywhere, all the time,” he stressed.

He said that while Norway had “significant disagreements with Iran on other issues, they also have the right to be protected as a state”.

Referring to Pakistan’s mediatory role in the ongoing conflict, he said he realised how difficult mediation and facilitation of parleys between the two sides could be.

“I know what a massive task you were taking on when you offered Islamabad not only as the venue but also as the facilitator of these talks,” he said, lauding Pakistan’s civilian and military leadership for their efforts.

“What you have been doing is really a service to the world, and hence, also to us.”

The Norwegian diplomat said Pakistan’s mediation efforts also mattered to his country as it was a large shipping nation.

“We share an interest in open sea lanes and the ability to trade in the high seas, and to respect the Constitution of the Oceans […] Whatever emerges from this tragic and unnecessary war in Gulf, we need to protect the principle of the free passage,” he explained. “And I am so happy we see completely eye to eye [on this],” he remarked.

The visiting minister added that his message to “anyone involved out there in the conflict is that this issue of free passage and an open strait is not an issue for the warring parties alone. It is a global issue that we have a shared interest in promoting”.

He said he had discussed other regional issues during the visit as well, ranging from the Kashmir issue to Afghanistan.

Moreover, Eide said, he was glad to learn more about a recently signed defence pact between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia in Makkah.

“These are three countries with whom Norway has very good and close relations,” he noted.

At the outset of his address, Eide said he was honoured to be in Pakistan, saying the last time a Norwegian foreign minister visited Pakistan was 10 years ago.

“So it was about time,” he remarked. “I promised you many months ago that I would come, and today, I live up to my promise. I was looking forward to this visit, which is short but very effective.”

Eide said there was a “strong partnership” between Norway and Pakistan, as well as the people of the two countries.

“We have a sizeable diaspora of Pakistani descent […] Many of them are in key positions of politics and society and are a very welcome contribution to our country; and the fact that we have so many people who know these two countries intimately is yet another argument for strengthening our economic ties,” he added.

The Norwegian foreign minister further said that Oslo and Islamabad were discussing strengthening economic ties “in the context of specifics” and enhancing trade ties in more structural ways.

He also mentioned climate change and floods in Pakistan, saying that the two sides agreed it was a foreign policy issue.

“And if you need one additional argument for stopping wars apart from relieving suffering and ending economic harm, it is that mankind should collectively try to focus on the real issues that require real cooperative action,” he said.

Eide said combating nature loss and climate change, promoting global health and fighting poverty were among the issues on his agenda for discussions during the visit.

Speaking earlier, Dar said the two countries had agreed to enhance bilateral ties and cooperation in all areas of mutual interest, including trade and investment, education, defence, climate change, information technology and maritime affairs.

He said Pakistan greatly valued its relations with Norway and looked forward to further strengthening them in the days, weeks and months ahead.

Dar also said bilateral political consultations (BPC) between the two countries had become a regular feature of their engagement. “We are looking forward to hosting the next round of BPC in Islamabad later this year in the winter,” he said.

Dar said the two sides also agreed that bilateral trade between Norway and Pakistan was “below the potential of both economies and needs to be enhanced through effective measures”.

“Pakistan offers enormous investment opportunities to Norwegian companies, and it is heartening to see many leading Norwegian companies investing in Pakistan.

“A renowned Norwegian company, Yara International, is establishing a joint venture in plant nutrition with the Fauji Fertiliser company. I hope this initiative will be a trailblazer for many more future projects between our two great countries,” he added.

Dar termed Pakistan’s partnership with Norway in the field of technology “a success story”.

“Pakistan’s IT exports to Norway have grown more than five-fold in the last two years, and I have no doubt that this is only the beginning.”

He further stated that the two sides also agreed on the expedient finalisation of various agreements and memoranda of understanding (MoU).

On climate change, he said there was a convergence of perspectives between the two countries.

“It is heartening to note that Pakistan and Norway signed the MoU under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement on April 1 this year,” he said, adding that the two sides also held talks on cooperation in maritime affairs.

He said he had told the visiting dignitary that Pakistan was “one of the world’s largest ship recycling facilities, and our strategic location makes it the most competitive and nearest recycling destination in this maritime region for ships coming from Norway”.

Dar thanked Norway’s maritime authorities for their support in capacity building and providing technical training for Pakistan’s shipbreaking industry in line with the Hong Kong International Convention.

He added that Pakistan and Norway had agreed to enhance people-to-people contact, which he said could become “defining for our relations and serve as social and cultural bridges between the two countries”.

The DPM said the two sides had also discussed labour mobility.

“We agreed to continue work on legal pathways for Pakistan’s skilled manpower, expressing the need to combat human smuggling and illegal migration. Both sides agreed that by providing safe, orderly and regular migration channels, we not only protect migrants’ rights and lives but also dismantle the illegal model of smuggling networks,” he elaborated.

Dar further said that both Pakistan and Norway shared a commitment to multilateralism, the principles of the United Nations Charter, respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity and the peaceful settlement of disputes.

“Our two countries remain actively engaged on issues related to the UN Security Council, and the two sides have strong convergence of views on major issues.

“Building on our previous experience of working together in international bodies and multilateral fora, both sides affirm their desire to continue mutual support and consultations on such forums.”

Dar said he had also briefed the Norwegian foreign minister and delegation on the Kashmir issue. He said he told them that India had added a new dimension to an already volatile security situation by unilaterally announcing the abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty in contravention of international law.

“We reiterate that India must end the weaponisation of water and uphold its treaty obligations under international legal obligations,” he asserted.

Dar said he had further briefed the Norwegian foreign minister on Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts for promoting dialogue, de-escalation and peaceful settlement of the US-Iran conflict. He thanked him for appreciating Pakistan’s role as a mediator in the conflict.

Moreover, he said, he had broadly discussed the Makkah defence pact with the visiting dignitary. “We had a great discussion, and it happens that all three countries enjoy the best of relations with Norway,” he said.

The DPM concluded his address, saying: “We agreed on the need to find peaceful solutions to the international conflicts in full respect of the principles of international law and the UN Charter.

“I thank his excellency, my dear friend, for his visit. I am confident that this visit will open a new chapter in Pakistan-Norway relations and will contribute to greater cooperation and mutual prosperity for the people of both countries in the years ahead.”

Delegation-level talks

Earlier in the day, Eide held delegation-level talks with DPM Dar, according to the Foreign Office (FO).

During the talks, the two sides reviewed the whole gamut of bilateral cooperation in various fields, including trade, investment, climate change, maritime affairs and education. They recognised the important role of the Pakistani diaspora in Norway and agreed to strengthen people-to-people ties between the two countries.

The two sides expressed satisfaction at the warm and cordial state of Pakistan-Norway relations and agreed to further deepen cooperation in areas of mutual interest,” it said.

FO said the two sides also held in-depth discussions on regional and international developments of mutual interest.

During the delegation-level talks, the visiting dignitary also recognised Pakistan’s role in the US-Iran war as “important and constructive”, lauding the leadership of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Field Marshal Munir and DPM Dar, as per the FO statement.

Eide had also appreciated Pakistan’s efforts to promote peace and expressed Norway’s desire to further strengthen bilateral ties earlier in the day in televised remarks.

He said Norway and Pakistan had a “very strong bilateral partnership”, adding that the presence of a large Pakistani community in Norway, which was “well integrated into Norwegian society”, had helped strengthen ties between the two countries.

“There are many leading politicians in Norway and many close colleagues who are actually of Pakistani-Norwegian descent, so it has really made a mark,” he said.

Eide said business ties between the two countries were also growing, particularly in the energy and fertiliser sectors, with Norwegian companies increasingly looking at opportunities in Pakistan.

He said Norway also saw opportunities for Pakistan to strengthen economic relations through its cooperation with Switzerland and Iceland, noting that the three countries could provide further avenues for expanding business relations.

Turning to the regional situation, Eide strongly commended the actions taken by Pakistan’s leadership.

Eide described the ongoing war as “incredibly dangerous” for global peace as well as the world economy, and praised Pakistan for stepping forward. He also appreciated Pakistan’s role in facilitating the Islamabad talks and maintaining engagement with the parties involved.

“I think it is fair to say that the position of Pakistan on the world stage, also in peacemaking, has really been strengthened by this commitment,” he said.

Eide said Norway was ready to assist Pakistan’s peace efforts, noting that Oslo had experience in peace negotiations and maintained open dialogue with both Tehran and Washington.

“Wherever we can be useful, we will,” he said.

He also highlighted Norway’s experience in international maritime affairs, saying the country was among the world’s major seafaring nations despite its relatively small population.

He said Norway could therefore play a constructive role in discussions concerning international maritime law and developments surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.

Dar, Eide discuss bilateral ties

The two ministers also held a “restricted-format meeting” earlier today, FO said.

“DPM Dar warmly welcomed Eide to Pakistan. The two ministers discussed the full range of bilateral relations, as well as regional and international developments, and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation in all areas of mutual interest,” according to FO.

Upon his arrival in Islamabad, Eide was received at the airport by Additional Foreign Secretary (Europe) Ambassador Ayesha Ali.

In a statement on Wednesday, the FO said the minister is undertaking the visit from Aug 13-14 at Dar’s invitation.

The visit is the first by a Norwegian foreign minister in a decade, the FO said, adding that the visit would build on high-level engagement between the two countries, including phone conversation between Dar and Eide in March and April, and the visit of Norway’s State Secretary Andreas Motzfeldt Kravik to Islamabad in May.

The FO stated that the visit would provide an opportunity to “further strengthen the longstanding and cordial relations between Pakistan and Norway and to explore new areas of mutually beneficial cooperation”.

World.title: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia will form political, military mechanisms to coordinate under defence pact, Ankara says
World.content:
Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia will form political and military mechanisms under a defence pact signed between the regional powers last week, Turkiye’s defence ministry said on Thursday, adding the alliance would also deepen defence industry cooperation.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed last week as the Middle East grapples with fallout from the US-Israeli war on Iran , which has dragged in regional players and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

At a weekly briefing in Ankara, the ministry said the mechanisms would include the three countries’ defence ministers, foreign ministers, and military chiefs.

It added that the joint military exercises were also being planned under the pact, while cooperation could include joint production and technology sharing in the defence industry.

The remarks come a day after Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said that he hoped more countries would join the agreement.

“Our vision for it is not limited to the three countries,” the Turkish leader told the London-based Asharq Al-Awsat daily.

“Rather, we aspire for it to grow, and perhaps appropriate conditions will emerge one day for all countries of the region to gather under its umbrella.”

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Saturday said Turkiye expected Egypt to join the pact “in the next stage”, telling the Anadolu state news agency only “a few technical issues” stood in the way.

Egypt has not commented on the agreement nor on the remarks by Fidan, who will visit Cairo on Thursday and Friday.

Kuwait , Bahrain and Somalia are among the countries that have welcomed it. Iran’s comments also took a rather positive tone, stressing its stance of pursuing “security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries”.

World.title: Dar orders intensified diplomatic engagement for release of Pakistani sailors held hostage by Somali pirates
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar directed “stakeholders” on Thursday to maintain close and regular coordination and intensify diplomatic engagement with national and international partners to facilitate the release of 10 Pakistani sailors who have been held hostage by Somali pirates since April.

The sailors were among the crew of the MT Honour 25, a Palau-flagged oil tanker that was hijacked by armed pirates off the coast of Puntland, Somalia, on April 21. Besides the 10 Pakistani crew members, the hostages also include seven Indonesians, including the captain, as well as an Indian and a Sri Lankan.

During more than three months of their captivity, there has been no progress either in negotiations or the payment of the ransom, said to be around $3 million, for their recovery.

Meanwhile, the Foreign Office (FO) has been saying that efforts continue for their release and return.

In a statement posted on X today, it said Dar chaired a high-level meeting to review Pakistan’s “intensified efforts” for the safe release of the sailors.

“The DPM/FM directed all relevant stakeholders to maintain close and regular coordination and intensify diplomatic engagement with national and international partners, including the Somali authorities and relevant international organisations, to facilitate the safe release of our citizens,” the FO stated.

The FO said the government remained “fully seized” of the situation and that Dar expressed hope that sustained and coordinated engagement would lead to a positive outcome and the seamen’s safe return.

It added that DPM Dar also expressed solidarity with the families of the sailors.

On August 7, more than 100 days after being taken hostage by Somali pirates, the crew members on board MT Honour 25 released another distress message in which they had appealed directly to the Pakistani government for their release.

In the two video messages, the Pakistani hostages and foreigners could be seen in a state of extreme distress, with most looking sick and weak. They requested that the Pakistani government talk to the Somali pirates and take steps to release them.

Since the hijacking, the crew has made several emotional videos and audio appeals , while reporting that they have run out of clean water, food and medicine.

The hostages are victims of an “ ownership crisis ”, as it is not clearly established who owns the ship and the man previously thought to be the owner was later revealed to be more likely a middleman who hired them.

Earlier, under the supervision of the Somali pirates, there were several videos and phone calls to the families of the hostages to pressure them to pay the ransom. But after mid-June, the messages had stopped, until the latest appeal.

World.title: Pakistan's first lunar rover named 'Jinnah-1': Suparco
World.content:
Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco) on Thursday announced “Jinnah-1” as the official name of the country’s first lunar rover.
